News.title: Trump’s $10bn BBC lawsuit to go ahead as judge rejects broadcaster’s bid to dismiss case over edited Panorama speech
News.content:
BEEB ROW Trump’s $10bn BBC lawsuit to go ahead as judge rejects broadcaster’s bid to dismiss case over edited Panorama speech







Next

DONALD Trump’s $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC will be allowed to proceed after a judge rejected a bid by the broadcaster to dismiss the case.

The US president hailed the ruling as a “huge victory against Fake News BBC” as he presses ahead with a controversial defamation case.

Trump, 80, is suing the broadcaster for a misleading Panorama edit of his speech on the day of the US Capitol riots on January 6, 2021.



He claims the corporation defamed him by “maliciously” editing his words to suggest he ordered his supporters to storm the Capitol.



The BBC denies the claims and has apologised for the error.

On Tuesday, judge Jeffrey T Kuntz rejected the BBC’s bid to dismiss the defamation suit – but quashed Trump’s claim that the edit violated Florida’s Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act.

Kuntz said in his ruling: “Whether President Trump can prove these claims and establish he sustained damages at summary judgment or trial is left for another day.”



Trump took to his social media platform Truth Social to celebrate the news, writing: “A Huge Victory against Fake News BBC, a terrible abuser of the truth, just handed down by highly respected District Court Judge, Jeffrey T. Kuntz, of the Southern District of Florida.”

He added: “We will continue fighting against, and defeating, all of those who try to deceive the American People!”

News.title: Moment helicopter carrying wedding guests spins out of control & crashes killing pilot, 43, while trying to land
News.content:
Next

THIS is the shocking moment a helicopter loses control and smashes into a field – tragically killing the pilot onboard.

Rafael Grossi Teixeira, 43, a seasoned helicopter pilot and trainer, was transporting wedding guests to a ceremony in Brazil’s Minas Gerais state.



On approach to the wedding venue, shocking footage shows the Robinson R66 chopper spiral erratically before hitting the ground on the afternoon of November 7.

Rafael and the five members of the wedding party were rescued alive from the helicopter wreckage and rushed to hospital.



Though Rafael was found initially conscious, his health deteriorated overnight and he succumbed to his injuries, according to Santa Casa Hospital.

One wedding guest is now being treated in intensive care, while four others remain hospitalised.



According to the Fire Department, the helicopter had been flying over the field as Rafael searched for a landing site.

The chopper had been just 65ft above the field when it started to lose control and subsequently plummets to the ground below.



Police are now carrying out forensic examinations of the crash site.

Brazil’s Air Force have also sent investigators to collect evidence and assess the circumstances that lead to the helicopter loosing control.

A father and experienced flyer, Rafael had been operating choppers for 20 years.

He previously worked for Brazil’s National Civil Aviation Agency (ANAC) which organised civil aviation schools.

He was involved in training centres, and oversaw examinations for those pursuing aviation.



The veteran pilot was also a founding partner of AR Aviation School, which started operating in March 2024.

The school teaches 13 practical training courses for both helicopters and aeroplanes.

In a statement, the school confirmed Rafael’s death and has expressed their condolences.

All training’s at AR Aviation School have been suspended indefinitely.

A funeral for Rafael was held on November 10. He leaves behind a son.

News.title: Chilling moment boy, 10, ‘points gun before shooting girl, 16, dead’ as mum rowed with neighbour about loud music
News.content:
Next

THIS is the chilling moment a boy points a gun before allegedly shooting a teenage girl dead as his mum brawled with neighbours over loud music.

Shocking footage shows the 10-year-old brandishing the weapon before opening fire during a violent Halloween clash.



Keinerlein Rangel, 16, was fatally shot after the boy’s mum, Elaina Gomez-Villeda, 40, allegedly warned neighbours that her son was “going to shoot you”.

The mum has been charged with murder after allegedly ordering her son to grab the gun as the furious row spiralled out of control.



The horror unfolded around 4pm when Gomez-Villeda confronted her neighbours over loud music blasting from their apartment complex in Albuquerque, New Mexico.

Security footage shows the mum, apparently dressed in a Day of the Dead costume, demanding they turn it down before a vicious brawl erupted.

She began trading blows with Keinerlein’s mum, Susana Rangel, as the two families clashed outside their homes.

Keinerlein was then seen fighting with Gomez-Villeda’s 10-year-old son before turning on his mum.

Amid the chaos, the boy dashed inside his apartment before returning armed with a handgun.

Horrifying footage shows the youngster firing two shots, with the first missing before the second fatally struck Keinerlein.



Albuquerque Police Detective Chase Jewell told a court that Gomez-Villeda could be heard shouting “get the gun” on security footage.

She also allegedly warned the family her son was “going to shoot you, look he’s going to shoot someone” before the teenager was killed.

Following the deadly shooting, Gomez-Villeda rushed her son back inside their apartment, where a six-year-old child was also present.



The pair barricaded themselves inside as the chaos continued outside.

Gomez-Villeda then called 911, claiming she had been attacked by her neighbours during the bitter dispute.

She also allegedly sent her husband a chilling text message reading: “I’m probably going to jail right now.”

Keinerlein’s devastated father arrived at the complex after the shooting and was told his daughter had been shot.

He then allegedly tried to smash his way into Gomez-Villeda’s apartment, breaking a window as she spoke to emergency services.



The mum later admitted grabbing a gun and firing at the furious father in a desperate bid to make him leave.

She told detectives: “I thought we were gonna die; these people, they do it a lot, and I didn’t think I was gonna be the target, but it is what it is.”

But the terrifying ordeal continued when armed cops descended on the apartment complex.

Officers reported seeing someone fire a weapon from inside the property, forcing them to scramble for cover.

Three people eventually emerged before Gomez-Villeda stepped outside clutching a handgun.



One cop opened fire at the armed mum, but the bullets missed and struck a pillar outside the building.

She eventually dropped the weapon and was taken into custody.

Gomez-Villeda appeared in Bernalillo County court on Friday, where prosecutors outlined the shocking allegations against her.

Her defence lawyer, Roberta Yurcic, argued that the boy had grabbed the gun after his mum was attacked with a drill and injured.

She insisted Gomez-Villeda had never ordered her son to open fire.



Yurcic said: “Despite the state really wanting those words to have been spoken, they’re not, by the detective’s review, she never tells him to shoot.”

But Judge Joseph Montaño rejected the defence’s arguments and ordered the mum to remain behind bars, warning that she posed a danger to the community.

He also expressed alarm at how comfortably the 10-year-old appeared to handle the deadly weapon in the footage.

Montaño said: “The fact that a 10-year-old is able to manipulate a revolver in the fashion in the video.”

He added: “How can the court fashion conditions of release for circumstances like this?”



Gomez-Villeda faces a string of serious charges, including murder, conspiracy to commit murder and child abuse.

She is also accused of contributing to the delinquency of a minor, negligently making a firearm accessible to a child, misdemeanour battery and receiving stolen property.

The accused mum remains locked up at the Metropolitan Detention Center without bond.

Her 10-year-old son has not been charged over Keinerlein’s death.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Prosecutors are reviewing whether the youngster can face criminal charges because of his age.



His identity has not been released by police.

News.title: M&S apologises as ‘mortified’ shopper ‘eats crispy MOTH’ lurking in her tortilla chips – ‘felt like a bushtucker trial’
News.content:
Next

M&S have apologised to a woman who was left “mortified” after finding a “crispy moth” in a bag of tortilla chips.

The customer said the experience felt “like she was in a bushtucker trial”, first mistaking the insect for a “burnt crisp.”



Suzanne Bailey, a mum-of-one from Liverpool, was dishing up a Mexican-themed spread for her family in October when she first caught sight of the crispy insect.

As part of the meal, the 45-year-old bought a bag of £1.25 Lightly Salted tortilla chips from Marks & Spencer.



After eating through around a third of the tortilla crisps, Bailey spotted what she thought was a “burnt tortilla at first.”

However, upon closer inspection, she was disgusted to discover a “crispy” moth which had been cooked with the rest of the crisps.

Suzanne said: “It [the moth] hasn’t just got in there after it’s been made, it’s been cooked.

“I put the tortillas into a separate bowl so we could scoop the mince [meat] up with.

“I actually thought the moth was a burnt tortilla at first.

“My daughter sat down and she had only eaten one tortilla [when I spotted the moth].



“I went to pick the burnt tortilla up and this is when I realised it was a moth.”

Stomach-churning photos of the crisp bowl show a lifeless bug on a bed of tortilla chips alongside its separated disembodied leg.



Fearing she may have actually eaten the creepy critter’s leg, the mum claims that her 13-year-old daughter, Isabella Bailey, threw up.

“My little girl had a mouthful of food and threw up,” she continued.

“I was mortified as I had eaten approximately a third of the bag.

“The moth was cooked, crispy and fried.

“It had an extensive coating of the seasoning on it.



“When I was putting all the tortillas into the bag [to keep as evidence] I spotted all of the moth’s legs.

” I was like, ‘how many legs have I eaten?'”

Suzanne has likened the experience to an eating challenge on I’m a Celebrity… Get Me Out of Here, calling the experience “gross and absolutely disgusting.”



“I’m not into bushtucker trials but it feels like I’ve done an M&S one.”

After being left £30 out of pocket after binning her £10 Mexican dinner and ordering a £20 takeaway, Suzanne submitted a formal complaint on the M&S website and called customer support.

Now, Suzanne says she has been put off eating tortilla crisps ever again and claims she will not shop at M&S in the future.

“We haven’t been back to shop at M&S,” she said. “I don’t think I could eat tortilla chips again either.

“We’re on holiday currently and we would always get nachos [but we wouldn’t now].”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

An M&S spokesperson has said: “We take matters like this extremely seriously and are working closely with our supplier partner to investigate this fully.

“We have been in touch with the customer directly to apologise for the inconvenience caused and offer a full refund.”

News.title: How Walliams went from ‘fat & ugly virgin’ to courting UK’s most beautiful women using chilling tactic HE boasted about
News.content:
Next

AT school David Walliams was the “fat ugly girl”, cruelly nicknamed Daphne who most people thought was gay.

It wasn’t until he was aged 20 and at university in Bristol that he finally lost his virginity to a fellow female aspiring thespian.



Having struggled for almost a decade after that to finally become famous, Walliams wasted no time in dating as many beautiful women as possible once he was in the limelight.

In 2004, the year after Little Britain transferred from radio to television, his dates included Liam Gallagher’s ex-Patsy Kensit and the models Lisa Snowdon and Abi Titmuss.

Other famous names romantically linked to the 55-year-old comedian are Spice Girl Geri Halliwell, Hollywood actress Kate Beckinsale and Made In Chelsea star Ashley James.



In the mid-noughties no party was complete without Walliams on the guest list.

He became pals with some of the biggest names in showbusiness, including Sir Elton John, and was often at glittering events.

There Walliams was often spotted chatting up women and leaving to engage in what he admitted were “casual sexual relationships.”

Now an investigation by ITV and The Guardian claims the former Britain’s Got Talent judge preyed on girls as young as 15 and harassed women in the workplace.

Walliams denies wrongdoing, insisting that he has never been a “sexual predator.”



Timeline of allegations 2003 The same year that Little Britain takes off, Walliams allegedly contacts 18-year-old model Lilly Creightmore. She later claims he targeted her while she was vulnerable. 2004 Walliams meets aspiring comedy writer Alex, then 15, at a Little Britain fan event. She hands him copies of her scripts and her contact details before he later calls her and offers work experience. They stay in touch through emails and phone calls over the following two years. 2005 Alex, then 17, says the tone of their relationship changes and Walliams begins asking her to send sexual photographs, including nude pictures. Walliams says he does not recall asking for such images and believed she was 18 at the time. 2006 Alex claims she first has sex with Walliams when she is 17. She says they slept together twice, including after she turns 18, but describes the encounters as pushy. Walliams denies grooming her and says he believed she was 18 during each encounter. 2007 Walliams contacts 15-year-old Jade through MySpace after she comments on a photograph of him, she claims. Jade claims he lifted her top and tried to put her hand down his trousers. She describes the alleged incident as grooming and a sexual assault. Walliams denies any sexual contact with her and rejects allegations of criminal activity. The same year, he also allegedly makes unwanted advances towards another young model, Ella, after getting her number through her agent. 2015 Walliams allegedly messages 17-year-old Abby Tomlinson on Twitter and invites her to a recording of Britain’s Got Talent. She attends with a 13-year-old girl and claims they are taken to his dressing room alongside two other teenagers. 2016 An 18-year-old woman, Sarah, claims she rejects Walliams after he tries to kiss her at his home. She also alleges he later tries to lead her towards his bedroom before her friend intervenes. Walliams denies forcing himself on her and says there was no sexual contact. 2017 A member of the Britain’s Got Talent production team, Mark, claims he found two “very young people” in Walliams’ dressing room while the comedian was wearing only a towel. 2022 Walliams leaves Britain’s Got Talent in November after recordings of derogatory and sexually explicit comments about contestants are leaked. 2023 Walliams takes the show’s production company, Fremantle UK, to the High Court over alleged misuse of private information and breaches of data laws. 2025 Walliams is dropped by publisher HarperCollins after reports of inappropriate behaviour towards young women at the company. One employee claimed she was in a consensual relationship with the author but believes he displayed an “abuse of power”. 2026 Walliams loses his High Court bid to block publication of the allegations and misses the deadline to appeal.

The best-selling author, though, has long spoken about his attraction to the opposite sex.

As he told Desert Island Discs in 2009: “I love women, I love being around women, I find them incredible and intoxicating.”

Growing up in leafy Banstead in Surrey, Walliams always wanted to make his emotionally aloof engineer dad Peter “proud.”

Instead it was his lab technician mum Kathleen who showered him with the affection he desired.

At school he didn’t receive the attention he craved.



While at the all-boys fee-paying Reigate Grammar his lack of sporting prowess stood out, with Walliams saying: “The way I ran, the way I threw a ball, the way I talked, the way I flicked my hair was just like a girl. In my case, a big fat ugly girl.”

At the Sea Scouts he said the boys would “fiddle with each other in the dark” in their tents.

And one of the men running the groups would chase them around the hall, spanking them.



Walliams commented: “My whole experience of sex at this time can be summed up in one word. Shame.”

In the sixth form at school, he mixed with girls but the one he most fancied only wanted to be his friend.

It wasn’t until he was aged 20 at Bristol University that Walliams first fell in love, reportedly losing his virginity to fellow student Katy Carmichael.

That relationship ended after Walliams moved to London, where he pursued his comedy writing career with Matt Lucas.

Before the duo broke through, Walliams began seeing the late star Caroline Aherne, who at that point was nationally famous thanks to The Royle Family.



Walliams said: “She was funny, northern and pretty in my favourite sort of way – blonde hair and big t**s.

“Of course I was aware of her troubled life, and like most men who were attracted to Caroline, I thought I could save her.”

That wasn’t to be.



During one drunken row, she told him: “You’ve got no love in your heart – you’re incapable of it.”

After a year together, the pair ended things just as his star began its ascendency.

It was in 2000 that Walliams got noticed on television, playing George Michael in sketch show Rock Profiles on UK Play and Little Britain first aired on Radio 4.

Lucas, though, was the most famous of the pair due to his regular appearance as George Dawes on Reeves and Mortimer’s show.

That quickly changed after Little Britain became a hit in 2003 on BBC 3.



Suddenly, Walliams was everywhere. Often seen leaving some swanky establishment with a well-known woman.

In January 2004 he was spotted leaving the home of Patsy Kensit, three years his senior.

They were called “the odd couple” because 6ft 2in tall Walliams, who was known for his “I’m a lady” sketch, seemed an unlikely love match with the blonde actress.



After that ended, he was seen out on the town with model and TV presenter Lisa Snowdon.

Walliams was later to describe Lisa as “Miss X”, the woman he had fallen in love with but left him heartbroken.

Lisa, 54, told The Sun: “Yes, It’s me. I’m Miss X. David and I are great friends and he’s such an amazing bloke, but there is no romance.

“David has made it clear he has feelings for me but we’ve got to a point where we can just have a platonic relationship.

“I’m very honest with him and he has been with me, so there are no games.”



Next Walliams got close to model Abi Titmuss, 50, who’d just come out of a relationship with John Leslie.

He was also linked in the press to, Martine McCutcheon, Suranne Jones, Ozzy Osbourne’s daughter Aimee, singer Lisa Moorish and Jayne Middlemiss.

All this rumoured high-powered dating led journalists to ask the star the questions – ‘how do you do it?’



In 2004 he answered: “Most women think I’m gay so I have a really easy time with them. They are lulled into a false sense of security.”

According to the Guardian, it was in January 2004 that he made contact with a 15-year-old aspiring writer they are naming Alex.

A couple of years later, by the time she was aged 17 they were allegedly in a sexual relationship.

In 2007, Walliams dated Halliwell, 54, for six weeks, who had been a close friend for years.

At this point all the women he’d been connected with were a similar age.



That changed when he was photographed kissing 18-year-old model Lauren Budd in a nightclub in February 2009

The theme continued when he pursued Dutch model Lara Stone later that year.

She was 13 years his junior and didn’t know who Walliams was, but that didn’t stop him.



Her dad Michael said: “The last thing she wanted was a boyfriend. But he was so persistent. Lara didn’t know who he was, but he was calling her all the time and sending flowers – so many flowers.

“He once filled his whole house with flowers as a surprise for her, and then, as a present, he gave her an A-Z guide of London with her initials printed on the front.”

In a whirlwind romance Walliams proposed marriage in January 2010 and they were hitched four months later.

The couple’s son Alfred was born in May 2013, but less than two years later the union was officially over.

It was around this point that a “heartbroken” Walliams allegedly messaged 17-year-old Abby Tomlinson on Twitter and invited her to a recording of Britain’s Got Talent.



Abby told ITV that she found herself in the star’s dressing room with three girls aged 13, 16 and 17.

In 2017 Walliams is said to have asked British model Chloe Ayling, famous for being kidnapped and 24 years his junior, to go on a date.

If there was a relationship it was short-lived.

That also seems to be the case for recent supposed romances with Pussycat Doll Ashley Roberts and former Page 3 model Keeley Hazell.

Any trysts Walliams has these days are kept private.



While he was often seen getting into cabs with glamorous women twenty years ago, he is seemingly less forward these days.

None of the accusations against him, which he denies, go beyond 2020.

And there is no suggestion any of his ex-partners were victims of any inappropriate sexual behaviour.

In his statement yesterday Walliams made it clear he has changed.

He said: “Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with.



“I realise I did not always take people’s feelings properly into account. That is something I regret.

“And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did.

“I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law.

“I am devastated that some of the women I met ten to twenty years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me.”

News.title: Missing 11-month-old found buried alive in DOG CAGE after rescuers hear faint cries coming from underground
News.content:
Next

AN 11-month-old baby has miraculously survived after being buried alive inside a dog cage for around 24 hours.

Little Koah Sharp was found “clinging to life” after rescuers heard his cries coming from beneath the dirt during a desperate search for the missing boy.



The horrifying discovery was made in South Carolina on Tuesday, just 50 yards from his paternal grandfather’s home.

Koah had reportedly vanished with his father, Michael Comer, 25, the previous morning, sparking a massive search involving more than 100 first responders.



Lexington County Sheriff Jay Koon described the heart-stopping moment officers heard the infant crying as they dug through freshly disturbed soil.

The baby had allegedly been trapped inside a two-by-two-foot wire dog crate, wrapped in a towel and buried in a shallow hole in woodland, the sheriff said.



Investigators believe the towel may have created a pocket of air that kept Koah alive underground.

“By the grace of God, [the crate] probably provided enough air for him to survive our estimation of the last 24 hours under that dirt,” Koon said, according to WIS 10.

The dramatic rescue unfolded after search teams spotted disturbed earth and pine straw about 50 yards into the woods.

As officers began digging, they suddenly heard the baby’s cries.



“So as you imagine, the race was on,” Koon recalled.

“Everybody’s getting down there trying to get him out.”

Koah was reportedly screaming as rescuers finally pulled from the cage.

“He was screaming at the top of his lungs, which is a good thing in the baby world, I would guess,” the sheriff said.

The infant was rushed to hospital, where he remained fighting for his life on Tuesday afternoon.



However, Koon said he was hopeful the boy would make a full recovery.

The nightmare began Monday morning when Koah was left in his father’s care while his grandmother, Trish Comer, ran an errand.

Another caregiver was due to arrive shortly afterward.



But when they reached the home, both father and son had vanished.

“By the time the caregiver got there, Michael was gone and Koah was gone with him,” Koon explained.

Relatives reported the baby missing that afternoon, triggering a frantic search across Lexington County.

Investigators reportedly found Koah’s belongings inside a home with both doors left open, but no sign of the pair.

Comer, who was not known to have a vehicle, was believed to have been getting rides around the county.



Police eventually tracked him down to an outbuilding in Batesburg late Monday night.

He was arrested on burglary and resisting arrest charges but offered little information about his son’s whereabouts, Koon said.

Koah’s devastated mother, Dezarae Sharp, claimed Comer had recently been allowed weekend visits with their son after attending therapy and giving up alcohol.

“His dad decided though it was time to get jealous over other guys, so he pulled this on this weekends’ trip,” she alleged, according to the Daily Mail.

Authorities said a motive remained unclear.



Comer remained behind bars Tuesday, with investigators considering additional charges connected to the baby’s disappearance.

He had reportedly been placed on probation just last month after pleading guilty to aggravated breach of peace.

The sheriff also confirmed previous domestic violence incidents involving Comer and Koah’s mother.

The U.S. Sun has reached out to the Lexington County Sheriff’s Department for more information.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

If you or someone you know is affected by any of the issues raised in this story, call or text the Childhelp National Child Abuse Hotline at 800-422-4453 or live chat at childhelphotline.org.



If a child or other person is in immediate danger, contact 911 immediately.

News.title: Brit tourist, 32, among nine killed in Poland shooting rampage is pictured as details of victims emerge
News.content:
Next

A BRIT tourist who was killed in a horror mass shooting in Poland has been pictured.

James Thomas Campbell, 32, died after a lone gunman opened fire at random while driving through Krakow’s packed main square.



Six people were shot dead and another 16 people were injured in the attack, including a second Brit, while cops later found three bodies inside the shooter’s family home.

A friend of James, who was a DJ from Scotland, told The Telegraph: “We are all in shock. This is too upsetting… we’re broken-hearted.”



A Foreign Office spokesperson told the outlet: “We are supporting the bereaved family and the family of another victim who has been injured.”

Michal Oksinski, 24, shot dead his mum, dad and sister in their beds before his shooting spree on Saturday, November 7.

The sick killer fired on crowds using an assault rifle while clad in military combat gear, according to police.

James was the second British casualty of the deadly massacre, shot along with Harry Marchant, 19, who was badly wounded in the ordeal.



The teen from York suffering a gunshot wound during the weekend shooting and is said to be in a stable condition in hospital.

Terrified tourists told how they ran for their lives as Oksinski sprayed the square with bullets – firing off 500 rounds of ammunition.

The massacre was the worst mass shooting Poland has seen in decades.



Sickening photos show bodies lying across the historic town centre as ambulance helicopters frantically airlifted the wounded to hospital.

A hero cop who tackled the shooter and suffered three gunshot wounds is among those in critical condition.

Victims from Portugal, Russia, Germany and Austria were also wounded while four Polish nationals – including a mum-of-four – lost their lives.

Police arrived on the scene within 23 seconds of the attack with cops gunning down the shooter three minutes later.

Oksinski later died in hospital of his injuries.



Government officials praised the speed of the recation for preventing a “much bigger massacre”.

Investigators are yet to establish a motive for the crime, with a probe set to clarify the circumstances of the attack.

Poland’s interior minister previously suggested that the assailant had been inspired by “far-right” views but the government later backtracked.



Government spokesperson Adam Szlapka said: “It is best to refrain from making comments, even if there are some initial indications.”

Police raided Oksinski’s home following the deadly rampage – and found the bodies of his mum Renata, 52 and dad Janusz, 53.

His 21-year-old artist sister, Magdalena, was also found dead and the family’s two cats had also been executed.

Each family member had multiple bullet wounds to the head.

Inside the shooter’s car cops uncovered two AR-15 assault rifles and two pistols with cops confirming that the gunman “had a firearms permit”.



Polish defence minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz described the massacre as a “terrible act of terror” while prime minister Donald Tusk said it was the worst case of terrorism that Poland had ever seen.

Authorities have yet to confirm whether the attack was terror-related.

Britain’s PM Andy Burnham says he is “shocked and saddened by the appalling shooting in Krakow”.

On Monday night thousands of mourners marched through the city square in a silent vigil for victims.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Heartbreaking photos show mourners placing candles at the spots where people were killed on Saturday.



Poland declared two days of national mourning as flags across Europe were flown at half-mast in memory of the dead.

News.title: Tragedy as woman, 27, dies from ‘mushroom poisoning’ after eating dried fungi bought from B&M in France
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

FATAL MEAL Tragedy as woman, 27, dies from ‘mushroom poisoning’ after eating dried fungi bought from B&M in France







Next

A YOUNG woman has died from suspected food poisoning after eating a pack of dried morel mushrooms bought from B&M.

Marie Lou, 27, developed severe gastrointestinal symptoms just hours after consuming the fungi in France.



She contacted her regional poison centre and was directed to hospital, where she received emergency treatment, according to reports.

However, her condition rapidly deteriorated and she died the following day.



Officials have stressed that a direct link between the mushrooms, her symptoms and the death is yet to be confirmed.

Prosecutors in Montpellier have launched a probe to investigate the cause of death.



An autopsy carried out at the city’s forensic institute confirmed that Marie-Lou had consumed the mushrooms shortly before the tragedy unfolded.

Her heartbroken family said in a fundraiser: “A judicial investigation is underway.

“Toxicological analysis will help us understand what happened, even if it will solve nothing.”

The mushrooms investigators believe Marie-Lou consumed were dried morels sold by popular discount retailer B&M.



A nationwide recall has since been issued for 60g packs of Champibon dried morel mushrooms carrying the barcode 3760201609743.

The warning covers all packets sold between October 12 and November 2 in France with a best-before date of December 1, 2029.

France’s Rappel-Conso service said the recall was triggered by the probable contamination of a batch with a toxin capable of causing food poisoning.



However, the recall does not confirm that the product caused Marie-Lou’s death.

There has been no finding of wrongdoing against B&M.

B&M has been approached for comment.

Marie-Lou’s family said they had planned for her to be cremated and her ashes stored in a family vault – but the court prevented the cremation because investigators may require further biological samples.

Her sister Julia Robert wrote: “We are going to lay Marie-Lou like a plant – she would have liked that.”



Marie-Lou’s family have launched an appeal to cover funeral costs estimated at €15,000.

A private burial is due to take place following a public ceremony at Grammont Funeral Home in Montpellier on November 13.

The tragedy comes after dozens of secondary school students including Brits were struck down by diarrhoea at a popular French ski resort.

Holidaymakers from the UK, Canada, Belgium and France – most of them teenagers – had to be evacuated and confined to a sports centre in La Plagne in April.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Nearly 100 of the children reported symptoms such as nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea, as well as several teachers.



Twenty firefighters and doctors were mobilised to deal with the fallout.

News.title: Mum of two, 44, reverses menopause symptoms by becoming medal-winning bodybuilder
News.content:
A mother-of-two who started bodybuilding at 40 is one of a growing number of women using the sport to banish symptoms of the perimenopause, according to medical experts. With studies showing the sport’s effectiveness in reducing hot sweats, Danielle Cooper, 44, who was also suffering with brain fog and fatigue, started bodybuilding after hearing it could help to temper her symptoms.

Now she has won multiple medals and feels healthier than she did 10 years ago. Danielle, from Southport, Merseyside, says: “I’ve won seven golds and a PCA Pro Card this year, which is like the holy grail of bodybuilding. But, even better than any title, is how bodybuilding has made me feel. At 40 I had debilitating symptoms of perimenopause, like brain fog, fatigue, lack of focus and night sweats. Now, at 44, they’ve gone - I feel better than I did in my 30s.”

Medical experts say more women have turned to bodybuilding in the last decade - with beating menopausal symptoms being a key consideration. Dr Brendon Stubbs, a physiotherapy researcher at King's College London, says: "It makes a lot of sense that women are taking up lifting around menopause.

View 7 Images A Swedish study had women lift three times a week for 15 weeks, and their hot flushes dropped by about 44% (Image: SHOWSHOOTS)

‌



“Once oestrogen drops, muscle and bone start going quicker and lifting weights is the best way we have to hold on to them. We've got decent trial evidence on hot flushes. A Swedish study had women lift three times a week for 15 weeks, and their hot flushes dropped by about 44%.”

The study found consistent resistance training over time improves the body's internal thermostat. Researchers at Linköping University found that strenuous lifting stimulates the release of endorphins in the central nervous system. This chemical release directly stabilises the hypothalamus, which is the brain's core temperature regulation centre.

Dr Stubbs says: “The women who didn't train saw no change at all. If you can't take HRT, or don't want to, that's worth knowing. Lifting helps with low mood too. There are over 30 trials on this now, and people who do strength training report fewer depressive symptoms. Low mood and poor sleep are really common around menopause, so that matters."

Danielle is just 5ft 3in and a size 6, but when flexing her muscles on stage she could rival Arnold Schwarzenegger. She says: “You’d never know when I’m in a hoody on the school run that there’s a rock hard six pack and bulging biceps under there. I’m incredibly strong - I can lift up my husband.”

‌



View 7 Images Danielle's six pack, which her two daughter's love

Danielle, who has two daughters, Sienna, 13, and Saffiah, 8, with her business owner husband, Wayne, runs an online coaching business for women. She says: “I’d been into fitness in my 20s, but then became a bit of a party girl and left the gym behind. Going into my 30s, I was a great mum, and a great wife - but I didn’t really look after myself, I was too busy looking after everyone else. Then perimenopause hit and the brain fog and hot flushes began. I felt rubbish.”

Her 40th birthday was a turning point. She says: “I wasn’t feeling great. I was perimenopausal and going through the motions of life. I knew something needed to change. I wanted to do something just for me.”

Having heard that bodybuilding was great for lifting the mood and general wellbeing, she found a local trainer - then entered her very first competition in secret in autumn 2024. She says: “I didn’t want anyone to know in case I was rubbish.” But Danielle came fifth - and fell in love with the sport. She says: “The buzz, the exhilaration … it was such a rush.”

‌



It is not, however, for the faint hearted. In the months before a competition - which sees entrants stand on stage in different poses, to highlight different muscle groups - a gruelling training regime and diet is required, for body builders to reach peak “stage lean”.

View 7 Images Danielle with husband Wayne and their daughters, Sienna, 13, and Saffiah, 8

Danielle says: “For five months before a show, I get up at 4.30am to do the first of two hour-long training sessions in the gym. I go to a pose coach to work on my positions and have had years of posing lessons. I watch what I eat and drink like a hawk, and taper down my calories as the show gets closer, to become as lean as I can. You want to see the muscle definition through the skin, the lines and ripples. That’s what ‘stage lean’ means.”

Several dark tans are also applied to highlight muscle tone. Danielle, who has her competition bikinis handmade in Manchester, says: “My girls love it, they think I look fabulous and so does Wayne - he’s incredibly proud of me. The girls say, ‘look at your muscles, Mummy, they’re massive!’”

‌



And Danielle says bodybuilding and how it’s changed her health - physically and mentally - is worth sacrificing ice creams around the pool on holiday and other unhealthy treats for. She says: “When I stand on that stage during a competition, I forget all that - it’s all worth it.”

In 2025, Danielle entered a second competition - and triumphed. She says: “I won my class and went on to come third in the universe. Not bad for a beginner! And not bad for a perimenopausal mum, either.

View 7 Images Danielle says: "I’ve found something that sets my soul on fire."

“The training brought my focus back,” she says. “My mind felt razor sharp for the first time in years. What’s more, I was sleeping better, had more energy and was truly happy. I’ve found something that sets my soul on fire.”

‌



This year, Danielle has competed across two federations, winning three British titles, seven golds and one PCA Pro Card. She says: “The PCA Pro Card sees you recognised as a credible athlete. It’s winning big.”

Danielle is currently riding high on her recent wins. And she has set her sights on a Universe Pro show, against contestants from all over the world, which kicks off in May 2028. She says: “I plan to take the crown.”

How to power up

Dr Brendon Stubbs shares everyday ways to start strength training. He says: “You don’t have to be a bodybuilder to reap the benefits in menopause. Anyone can start using strength training to reduce symptoms.”

View 7 Images Dr Brendon Stubbs, a physiotherapy researcher at King's College London (Image: © feelimage/Felicitas Matern)

‌



No gym needed: “Squats, sit-to-stands from a chair, press-ups against the worktop and lunges all count.”

Twice a week: “Two sessions a week working your legs, back, chest and arms is a good start. Three is better.”

Make it hard: “The last few reps should be a struggle. Build the weight up bit by bit.”

Short bursts: “A few minutes of squats while the kettle boils adds up.”

Carry more: “Take the heavy shopping bags, carry the washing upstairs, park further away.”

Give it time: “In the trials, women saw changes after about 15 weeks.”

Get help early: “A few sessions with a coach or physio is money well spent. If you have osteoporosis or pelvic floor problems, get advice first.”

Menopause benefits

Dr Nighat Arif, resident doctor on ITV's This Morning and author of The Power of Menopause & Midlife, says body building and weight training both benefit women facing the perimenopause and menopause.

View 7 Images Dr Nighat Arif, author of The Power of Menopause & Midlife

She says: “Bodybuilding and strength training overlap significantly and use much of the same equipment can help look after your muscles and bones. It’s about staying strong for everyday life, now and in the years ahead.”

‌



Dr Arif says all kinds of exercise are helpful in overcoming menopausal symptoms. She explains: “It's important to understand exercise isn’t a magic fix for menopause, but it can help with some of the things that make it feel so hard, such as poor sleep, low mood and tiredness. It’s about feeling better in yourself.”

And for those who don’t want to commit to the rigorous body building work outs, there are softer options. She says: “Movement doesn’t have to mean a punishing workout. A walk, a swim or some strength exercises all count. Find something you enjoy and can keep coming back to.”

News.title: Andy Burnham vows to unveil 10-year plan to transform Britain before Christmas
News.content:
Andy Burnham vows to unveil 10-year plan to transform Britain before Christmas

The Prime Minister stepped into Downing Street pledging a decade-long scheme to reverse '40 years of neoliberalism', and lift Britain back to where it should be

View 2 Images Andy Burnham promised the plan before Christmas (Image: House of Commons/UK Parliament/Press Association)

Andy Burnham has promised to unveil his 10-year plan to transform Britain before Christmas.

‌



‌



The PM stepped into Downing Street pledging a decade-long scheme to reverse “40 years of neoliberalism”, and lift Britain back to where it should be.

‌



Mr Burnham had previously suggested the plan could be delayed until the New Year, but has now promised it sooner to give the country “stability” after 14 years of Tory chaos.

‌



Challenged by Kemi Badenoch at PMQs on when the plan was coming, he said: “I did walk up Downing Street promising a 10-year plan for this country, because I am determined to give this country the stability that they failed to provide.

View 2 Images Kemi Badenoch clashed with Andy Burnham at PMQs (Image: Getty Images)

“I am determined to give the leadership that this country needs, and I can say to her, we will present our plan for Britain to this House before it rises for the Christmas recess.”

‌



“We are facing the big issues, and we will lay that out in the 10-year plan before this country. This country was going backwards under the party opposite. We are leading it forward. We are bringing people back together. We are giving people hope. She is voting against the help that we've just announced in the budget. When is she going to directly address the cost of living crisis in this house?”.

Mr Burnham has billed the plan as his defining blueprint for what he wants to achieve, including establishing a national care service, slashing bills, and finally bringing utilities under public control.

‌



The plan is reportedly being written by former Keir Starmer aide Peter Hyman, though officials insist it will be the PM himself who makes the key decisions.

It came in a session that also saw Mr Burnham skewer the Tory leader over her criticism of the budget, and Conservative opposition to tax cuts.

Article continues below

He said: “Can I just say she mentions the budget, the most popular budget I have to say for a number of years, that helped people with the cost of living crisis. And can she explain, can she explain why they voted against a bank levy that will deliver a council tax cut for 20 million households in January?”.

Last week Mr Burnham told The Economist the plan would be even more radical than people think. He said: “I will lay out my very clear vision for Britain, and it will be substantial, and it will also be, in my view, compelling because I am weaving the different threads together.”

News.title: How broadband delays cause 'Wi-Fi rage' - and could ruin your Black Friday deals
News.content:
How broadband delays cause 'Wi-Fi rage' - and could ruin your Black Friday deals

With millions hunting online bargains, experts warn slow speeds could cost shoppers money as patience runs out in seconds.

It takes only 12 seconds to trigger 'Wi-Fi rage' when a webpage stubbornly refuses to load, according to new research. A survey of 2,000 adults revealed they have just eight seconds of patience before frantically hitting refresh in a bid to get things moving. On average, however, tempers begin to fray by the fourth attempt.

‌



Overall, two-thirds of adults have fallen victim to 'Wi-Fi rage', with broadband speed and connectivity issues becoming a persistent source of frustration for many. Among those affected, 34% said they encounter it several times a week. The biggest culprits include freezing video calls (39%), failed payments (29%) and crucial TV moments buffering (29%).

View 3 Images One in three experience 'Wi-fi' rage multiple times a week (Image: Getty Images)

Many people lose their cool when forced to use their smartphone as a hotspot due to broadband problems (16%), while the same number see red when they get booted out of an online game.

Bedrooms proved to be the worst signal blackspot in the home (35%), while 11% struggle to maintain a connection while scrolling in the bathroom.

The research was commissioned by Community Fibre to mark the launch of its Black Friday sale, which will see new customers double their broadband speeds for the same cost.

View 3 Images They have little patience when it comes to slow internet (Image: Getty Images)

Peter Rampling, a spokesperson for the London-based broadband provider, said: "These findings underline just how fundamental reliable broadband has become to everyday life and how frustrating it can be when your Wi-Fi doesn't deliver.

"People now depend on their connection for everything from working and making payments to entertainment and staying in touch, so interruptions can have a significant impact.

"For London households, having fast, consistent connectivity throughout the home is no longer simply a nice-to-have. It's an essential part of how we live, work and relax."

View 3 Images Poor internet could affect snapping up Black Friday deals (Image: Getty Images)

With Black Friday just around the corner, 48% of people believe that dependable Wi-Fi is crucial to bagging the best deals, helping them steer clear of checkout issues (59%) and keep stress levels down while shopping (41%).

The hunt for bargains has also seen 21% take a break from work specifically to buy an item, while 19% have set alarms for the early hours of the morning to make sure they don't miss out.

With 37% planning to make a purchase during Black Friday or Cyber Monday this year, 57% will be scouring the sales for Christmas presents, while 29% hope to secure household essentials.

And a reliable connection is more important than ever, with 85% claiming Wi-Fi has become a necessity rather than a luxury, according to the stats by OnePoll.

Peter Rampling, from Community Fibre, added: "With demand on home broadband continuing to grow, households need a connection that can keep pace.

"Our Black Friday offer is an opportunity for Londoners to get an even faster connection that will deliver around the clock.

"And with support to help with any termination fees from your previous provider, now is a great time to switch."

News.title: Woman uncovers aunt's heroic WWII effort to hide stranded commandos from Nazis
News.content:
Woman uncovers aunt's heroic WWII effort to hide stranded commandos from Nazis

79-year-old Liz Walton discovered her aunt sheltered British soldiers on occupied Guernsey while German troops lived next door.

Liz Walton discovers her auntie's hidden history

A woman has discovered the amazing wartime role her auntie played when she risked her life hiding British commandos during WW2.

‌



‌



Liz Walton, 79, discovered her auntie Ada Le Poidevin sheltered three British soldiers after they were left behind during a raid on Nazi-occupied Guernsey in 1940, despite German troops living next door.

‌



In July that year, Corporal Dennis Dumper, Private Fred Drain and Private Andrew Ross were left stranded on the island without food or shelter. Ada and her husband Walter stepped in, hiding them in their garden shed despite the potentially severe consequences if they were discovered.

‌



View 7 Images Liz was shocked to hear about her aunt's history (Image: © SWNS)

Liz said: “There were huge risks because there were Germans living next door, and people were being sent off to concentration camps – they were terrified of being caught.

“It must have been absolutely horrendous for people like my aunt, who had been involved in the First World War just relatively few years before, and then 20 years later to have the Germans actually in their homes.”

‌



After several days, the soldiers realised they had little choice but to surrender to the Nazis and were taken as prisoners of war.

All three survived the conflict and later moved to London, but remained close to Ada and Walter, regularly returning to Guernsey to visit them and even attending the couple's Golden Wedding celebration.

‌



It was the second time Ada had put herself in danger during wartime, having spent two years supporting British troops in France during WW1, where camps she worked in came under enemy fire and suffered heavy shell damage.

View 7 Images Ada Le Poivedin on top of a WW1 Tank (Image: © SWNS)

‌



View 7 Images Ada Le Poivedin (Right) stood in the ruins of Arras in France (Image: © SWNS)

Now her story has been pieced together by Liz using a treasure trove of photographs and diaries alongside records on Ancestry.com.

‌



The retired teacher, from Guernsey, carried out “detective work” to match her aunt's personal accounts and photographs with official wartime records.

Liz had been fascinated by Ada’s stories since childhood and inherited her collection of diaries and photographs when she died aged 88.

‌



Simon Pearce, military genealogist at Ancestry.com, said: “Stories like Ada’s are an incredibly powerful reminder of the courage and sacrifice shown by ordinary people during extraordinary times.

“Being able to uncover these moments and keep them alive means future generations can understand not just what happened, but the people and families behind our shared history.

‌



“So many remarkable wartime stories are still waiting to be discovered, often within our own family histories.”

View 7 Images A WW1 post card from Ada (Image: © SWNS)

‌



Ada was born in Guernsey in 1895 and volunteered for the Salvation Army in France in 1917, while still in her early 20s. “There were no men in our family that could go and fight, she felt a calling to go”, Liz said.

She spent two years in British camps, providing refreshments to soldiers, writing letters for them and mending their clothes.

‌



Ada travelled to areas including Abbeville and Amiens, where fighting was heavy, and the camps she worked in were on more than one occasion fired upon and badly damaged by shells.

After the war, she contracted Spanish flu and was hospitalised in Wimereux, near Boulogne, but recovered and went on to work with the Salvation Army's Graves Visitation Service.

‌



For four years, she helped bereaved families travel to France to visit the graves of loved ones killed during the conflict.

View 7 Images The documents Ada received when she went to WW1 (Image: © SWNS)

‌



View 7 Images Ada's passport when she went to WW1 (Image: © SWNS)

Liz added: “Most of the graves were just wooden crosses that anybody had put up, because they hadn't started making proper cemeteries yet.

‌



“She took them through Arras, where everything had been blown up and completely destroyed.

“I went there in the 1970s and showed her some pictures of it and she burst in to tears as she never thought she would see it rebuilt.”

‌



When families were unable to make the journey themselves, Ada would visit soldiers' graves on their behalf, leaving flowers, taking photographs and pressing flowers to send home to their relatives.

Ada told Liz she was given a silver medal for her Salvation Army service, although Liz has never been able to track it down.

‌



She returned to Guernsey in 1923 and married Walter Bourgaize five years later, with the couple going on to run Torteval Stores together.

View 7 Images Ada's Salvation Army medal (Image: © SWNS)

‌



Liz said: “As a person, Ada was immensely kind and caring. She was always immaculately dressed. She would help anyone in need and loved having children around her even though she had none of her own.

“She and Walter lived very modestly in a small, rented house without electricity, mains water or proper drainage for much of their life.”

‌



Reflecting on her aunt's contribution, Liz said: “I don't think many people are aware of how many women were directly involved in the First World War and how it changed the role of women in society.

“They nursed the wounded, cooked for the troops, acted as clerks and dispatched riders to aid communications. Women became used to earning their own money and being independent so domestic service was no longer an attractive option.

Article continues below

“Women's war work was life changing not just for them but for everyone.”

News.title: New coffee discovery as study links drink to two physical changes
News.content:
New coffee discovery as study links drink to two physical changes

The study's main discovery is that regular coffee consumption is linked to measurable physical changes

View 3 Images Frequent coffee drinkers showed more active muscle contractions in the colon (Image: Getty)

For many people, a cup of coffee in the morning can prompt a bathroom visit, but this doesn’t happen to everyone. Research suggests coffee encourages bowel movements in roughly one-third to two-thirds of people. Its effect can depend on how quickly your gut moves, how sensitive you are to caffeine, and whether you drink it with food, which can activate the body’s natural digestive reflexes.

‌



‌



Now, new research from the University of Copenhagen offers a fresh look at how coffee actually interacts with the human digestive system. Published in November 2026 in the journal Gut Microbiology, the study tracked 61 healthy Danish adults over nine days to examine how regular coffee consumption affects the gut.

‌



While earlier studies relied mainly on stool samples to examine gut bacteria, the Copenhagen researchers took a groundbreaking approach. They asked participants to swallow a tiny wireless sensor capsule that measured internal acidity, pressure, transit time, and muscle movements in real time as it travelled through the digestive tract.

‌



View 3 Images New research from the University of Copenhagen reveals that regular coffee drinking is linked to measurable physical changes inside the human digestive tract (Image: Getty)

The study's main discovery is that regular coffee consumption is linked to measurable physical changes inside the gut, alongside a wider variety of gut bacteria. Specifically, researchers found two key physical effects:

More frequent colon contractions A more acidic small intestine

‌



Participants with higher levels of caffeine breakdown products in their urine experienced more active muscle contractions in their colon. This helps keep intestinal muscles working and moves waste along.

Frequent coffee drinkers, defined as those having one to five cups a day on more than three days a week, had a lower pH, meaning higher acidity, in their small intestine compared to rare drinkers. Scientists noted that while acidity in the small intestine plays a key role in breaking down food, it is not yet clear whether this shift is helpful or harmful.

‌



View 3 Images :Researchers used a swallowable wireless sensor capsule to measure internal acidity, pressure, and muscle contractions in real time as it travelled through the digestive system

Ensure our latest headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as a Preferred Source in your Google search settings

‌



"Frequent coffee consumption appears to affect the physiology of the gut itself, in other words, how the gut functions," first author Francesca Bucci, a PhD student at the Department of Nutrition, Exercise and Sports at the University of Copenhagen, said.

However, the findings also help explain why a single cup of coffee might not relieve constipation on demand. Despite the extra colon contractions, overall transit time through the digestive tract did not change dramatically between frequent and rare drinkers.

Article continues below

Because the study observed everyday habits in a small group rather than running a controlled trial, it cannot prove coffee alone caused these effects. For reliable daily regularity, experts still recommend drinking plenty of water and eating fibre-rich foods.

News.title: M25 traffic live: Man injured as horror pile-up sparks severe delays near Junction 11
News.content:
National Highways has warned of 'severe delays' of more than 90 minutes after a multi-vehicle crash on the M25 in Surrey

There are severe delays on the M25 in Surrey following a crash involving three vans and a lorry, which left one man injured.

The collision happened at around 6.55am on the clockwise carriageway between junction 11 (Chertsey) and junction 12 (Thorpe).

South East Coast Ambulance Service confirmed the man was treated at the scene for a leg injury before being taken to St George's Hospital in London for further treatment.

Three of the carriageway's four lanes were closed following the crash, with motorists facing delays of more than 90 minutes. All lanes have since reopened, but delays of around an hour remain.

News.title: Four children among seven injured after car ploughs into pedestrians in Glasgow
News.content:
Four children among seven injured after car ploughs into pedestrians in Glasgow

Police Scotland has confirmed four children were among six pedestrians taken to hospital after a car ploughed into a group of people on Hyndland Road in Glasgow.

View 3 Images A car surrounded by police cordons following a crash involving pedestrians on Hyndland Road in Glasgow. (Image: Andrew Milligan/Press Association)

Four children were among seven people injured after a car ploughed into pedestrians in Glasgow, with six taken to hospital for treatment.

‌



‌



The crash happened on Hyndland Road in the city's West End at around 3.45pm on Tuesday, November 10.

‌



In an update on Wednesday, Police Scotland confirmed that a 34-year-old woman and a 23-year-old man suffered serious injuries.

‌



A 13-year-old boy, a 12-year-old girl and two 13-year-old girls are all described as being in a stable condition.

View 3 Images Police at the scene of the collision involving pedestrians in Glasgow's West End. (Image: Andrew Milligan/Press Association)

Donald Trump lashes out at Republican 'loser' in tantrum over Hegseth impeachment attempt READ MORE :

The 29-year-old male driver was treated by paramedics at the scene.

‌



The road remained closed until around 11.30pm on Tuesday while emergency services dealt with the aftermath of the collision.

Police Scotland said enquiries remain ongoing, although officers do not believe any criminality was involved.

‌



View 3 Images The crash happened on Hyndland Road in Glasgow's West End on Tuesday afternoon. (Image: Andrew Milligan/Press Association)

Inspector Ryan Curran, from the Greater Glasgow Road Policing Unit, said: "Our investigation into this crash remains ongoing, although there is not believed to be any criminality.

Article continues below

"We are appealing for anyone who witnessed the crash, or who was in the area around the time and may have dash-cam or other relevant footage to come forward."

Anyone with information is urged to contact Police Scotland on 101, quoting incident number 1955 of November 10.

News.title: Brits' Christmas spending plans - from £1,000 budgets to buying gifts for themselves
News.content:
Brits' Christmas spending plans - from £1,000 budgets to buying gifts for themselves

Research has given a snapshot in just how much Brits expect to spend on Christmas, and what they'll be buying

View 3 Images Gifts are the biggest single outlay at Christmas, survey says, but spending plans vary widely (Image: Getty Images)

Around one in 10 people expect to spend less than £100 on Christmas this year, research by Lloyds bank has revealed.

‌



‌



At the other end of the scale, its survey also showed how 7% plan for splash out more than £1,000.

‌



The findings come from snapshot poll into what the nation’s spending habits are likely to be this festive period, with implications for retailers and other businesses, as well as the wider economy.

‌



In the face of a worsening cost of living squeeze, one in four people expect their Christmas bill will be bigger this year, which could be a result of higher prices or loosening the purse strings. That said, around two fifths reckon they will spend about the same, and about a fifth of people think this Christmas will be cheaper than the previous one.

View 3 Images A fifth of Brits say they plan to treat themselves this Christmas (Image: Getty Images)

Some 13 million adults won't have enough money this Christmas to pay even essential bills READ MORE :

Waitrose Christmas advert sees Keira Knightley and Joe Wilkinson marry READ MORE :

The most typical festive budget is £250 to £499 (23%), followed by £100 to £249 (20%). A further 28% expect to spend £500 or more. Around a fifth (18%) don’t know how much they’ll spend.

‌



Presents for family and friends are the biggest Christmas expense for three in five (60%) people. However, a sizeable 26% of those quizzed say they are not expecting to spend any money on gifts this year. It is not just about others, it seems. A fifth of those in the survey say they plan to buy something for themselves.

Pets are also very much part of people’s plans, as one in five expecting to buy gifts or treats for their animal companions.

‌



While most people look forward to Christmas, it can put considerable added financial strain on families. Many resort to putting purchases on credit cards, which can lead to a debt hangover in the new year. Yet many people are better - or able - to plan ahead by spreading the cost of Christmas.

View 3 Images One in five people to buy gifts or treats for their animal companions this Christmas (Image: NBCU Photo Bank via Getty Images)

‌



According to the survey, nearly a third (31%) of people have been putting money aside each month, while 28% still plan to use their December pay packet.

Others are likely to use the Black Friday discounting event at the end of November when retailers, in theory, will slash their normal prices.

‌



A recent report from discount website VoucherCodes estimated shoppers will spend record £9.8billion across the Black Friday weekend, up 3% from 2025. Spending will predominantly be driven by a forecast £5.3bn worth of online sales, although it predicts £4.5bn will go through high street tills.

Almost two-thirds of Brits now see Black Friday as a way to make a saving - nearly double the 35% from last year.

‌



Scepticism is also fading, with the number of people saying the deals are ‘a scam’ dropping from 18% last year, to just 4% this year.

Clair Hughes, savings expert at VoucherCodes.co.uk, said: “Black Friday is fast approaching and this year the sales event is bigger than ever. With Christmas just around the corner, it has become a staple in my calendar when it comes to getting the most out of dwindling festive budgets and seemingly unaffordable Christmas wishlists.

Article continues below

“In fact almost 45% of Black Friday shoppers will use the sales for their Christmas shopping.”

News.title: Jonathan Ross 'horrified' by Walliams allegations and Brand conviction
News.content:
TV presenter Jonathan Ross has said he is "horrified" by allegations of sexual misconduct against David Walliams and the rape conviction of Russell Brand.

In a statement, Ross said he was once "on friendly terms with both men", but that at the time he was "genuinely unaware of their conduct".

ITV News and the Guardian on Tuesday published reports alleging that Walliams has been accused of sexual misconduct by several women. Walliams denies all the allegations against him. Brand was sentenced to 10 years in jail for rape on Monday.

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said that the allegations against Walliams were the "latest in a long line of reported abuses of power" in the media.

Some of the women accuse Walliams of "grooming" them when they were teenagers, or allege other inappropriate behaviour.

In a letter to journalists published by the Guardian, Walliams said he was "not a sexual predator" and had not "broken the law".

If you are affected by any of the issues in this story, help and support is available at BBC Action Line.

In his statement, Ross also addressed a joke he made at a comedy awards show in 2004, in which the punchline suggested Walliams would be "going home" with a 15-year-old.

Ross acknowledged the controversial quip and described it as "tasteless".

He added: "This joke was submitted to me by the Comedy Awards script writing team and I believed that the punchline was a reference to the fact he had publicly dated younger women, exaggerated for comic effect.

"Had I had any reason to suspect that it might be referring to actual events, I would not only have refused to use it, but I would not have felt comfortable continuing a personal or professional relationship with him."

Ross is one of the country's best-known TV presenters, having regularly hosted celebrities on his Jonathan Ross Show, including David Walliams and Russell Brand.

He said he was "as horrified by the revelations about David Walliams and the crimes of Russell Brand as the rest of the nation".

He added: "My thoughts are with the many, many women who have bravely come forward."

The allegations include:

News.title: 'I felt like I was being manipulated': Woman alleges Walliams groomed her as a teenager
News.content:
Lilly Creightmore, who has alleged Walliams "groomed" her as a teenager, has told BBC Newsnight that she was "angry" at his behaviour.

She said that Walliams invited her to move in with him while she was "in between living situations". She was 18 at the time. She says she "felt instantly pressured to share a bed with him" but told him she was not interested in him in a romantic way.

After about a week of refusing Walliams's advances, Creightmore said "he started to become very moody and rude and cold".

According to ITV, Walliams says he did not act inappropriately and did not "target" her because she was "vulnerable" or "young".

TV agent Dermot McNamara, who has represented someone allegedly groomed by Walliams, told BBC Newsnight he had informed "authorities and broadcasters" about Walliams's alleged "inappropriate behaviour" but no action was taken.

Walliams denies all allegations, and in a statement to journalists shared by the Guardian said he was "not a sexual predator" and had not "broken the law".

He acknowledged that "at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with" and said he regretted not always taking "people's feelings properly into account".

News.title: UK falls silent to mark Armistice Day
News.content:
The UK has fallen silent on Armistice Day, commemorating the end of World War One and to remember those who have died in conflicts.

A national remembrance service took place at the Cenotaph in London, with ceremonies and a two-minute silence observed in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting laid a wreath at the Cenotaph, which was also attended by senior military figures, children and cadets.

In Staffordshire, the Duke and Duchess of Gloucester laid a wreath at the Royal British Legion National Remembrance Gardens.

Hundreds of people gathered at the Armed Forces memorial in the gardens, formerly known as the National Memorial Arboretum.

Geoffrey Spencer, 101, who joined the RAF in 1943, was among the veterans attending the event.

Those who served in more recent conflicts, from the Falklands to Afghanistan, were also present.

News.title: Police told Russell Brand to leave Jemima Goldsmith's house in 2014
News.content:
Police have confirmed they told Russell Brand to leave his ex-girlfriend Jemima Goldsmith's house in 2014 after she claimed a violent incident took place.

Thames Valley Police said officers were contacted by an alleged victim and went to an address in Oxfordshire on 25 July 2014 but no arrests were made.

They listened to her concerns and gave support, and "also ensured the victim's partner left the address, as per the victim's wishes", the police added in a statement on Wednesday.

Goldsmith, who dated Brand for about a year, wrote on X on Monday that she "had to call the police to have him removed from my house in 2014 during a violent incident" but chose not to press charges.

Brand was jailed for 10-and-a-half years for rape and sexual assault on Monday.

In her post, 52-year-old Goldsmith said she was "in awe of the courageous women who came forward at Brand's trial" and was "glad and relieved" he had "finally faced justice".

She wrote: "I have had my own personal experience of his violence, coercive control and abuse.

"I had to call the police to have him removed from my house in 2014 during a violent incident."

The Press Association reported that Goldsmith had asked for Brand to leave the property, her wish was then communicated to him by police, and he agreed to leave the house.

Goldsmith added: "I chose not to press charges at the time and not to go public with this, as I was worried about the impact of the press attention on my then teenage children.

"I have neither seen nor spoken to Brand since that period in 2014. Whilst my pain in relation to this, pales in comparison to what the women have testified in court have suffered, this was a difficult period in my life which has had a lasting impact."

She also said she had "assisted the journalists who finally exposed him", and had been willing to testify to his "abusiveness" if they were sued.

TV producer Goldsmith is also the former wife of ex-Pakistani prime minister and cricketer Imran Khan, the daughter of late billionaire entrepreneur Sir James Goldsmith and sister of ex-Conservative government minister Zac Goldsmith.

News.title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive
News.content:
A British man who was charged with spying for China has told the BBC he was a "convenient fall guy" for UK police and security services who wanted to put espionage threats by foreign states "on the map".

Chris Cash, a former parliamentary researcher, has shared more than 6,000 messages with us revealing how a Chinese official sought information about sensitive political matters in the UK - including the 2022 Tory leadership battle to decide the next prime minister.

The messages show how Cash's friend in China, Chris Berry - with whom he had been sharing information - dramatically described a "secret" meeting between Berry and a high-ranking Chinese official.

Berry said he had been told that China was concerned about how a British MP it had sanctioned might be promoted to a cabinet role.

The messages also reveal how Cash used his friend as a reference during vetting for a parliamentary pass - which was approved.

Like Cash, Berry was also charged with espionage. The two men consistently maintained their innocence.

In Cash's first interview since his acquittal, which sparked a political row over the government's failure to designate China as a "threat", he says he would "never do anything" to harm UK national security.

But he admits he was "unprofessional and naive" to send "gossiping" texts to his friend, whom he met in 2018 when they both taught English in a school in China.

Although the trove of messages shows him discussing sensitive topics, there is no evidence in them that Cash was paid by, or sympathetic to, the Chinese Communist Party.

News.title: Prince George's artwork featured in Country Life magazine
News.content:
Elsewhere in the edition, Catherine, who revealed two years ago that she was receiving cancer treatment, discussed her recovery journey.

Speaking with nature writer Robert Macfarlane, she said: "I was told in hospital that my recovery would not be linear.

"There will be good days and bad days, that it will take time.

"This is the same in nature. It shows us that periods of rest, reflection and renewal are equally as important as moments of growth."

Prince William discusses walks with the family's dogs, Orla and Otto, and how his children love to go outside and explore. He also tells of his fondness for a pub visit and a pint of cider with ice.

Aston Villa manager Unai Emery is also featured in the magazine, and described the prince's support for the club as "fantastic" ahead of publication.

"If we can give him good news, good results or good moments in football, we are proud of it," he said in a video.

Another prominent part of the Country Life edition, published this week, is Prince William setting out his drive to ensure women in the British armed forces feel safe.

The Prince of Wales called for a military culture that is more inclusive and respectful of women, saying that more must be done to ensure women in the military are shown respect and protected from sexual harassment.

It follows the death of 19-year-old soldier Jaysley Beck in 2021. A coroner ruled the Army's failure to take action - after Gunner Beck was harassed by her line manager and sexually assaulted by another colleague - had contributed to her suicide.

Prince William is not the first senior royal to guest edit Country Life.

The King has guest edited the magazine on several occasions, including to mark his 65th and 70th birthdays. Queen Camilla and Anne, the Princess Royal, have also previously edited editions.

News.title: Vinícius Jr's message to Sudan boy who received prosthetic legs after BBC report sparked appeal
News.content:
Real Madrid footballer VinÃ­cius JÃºnior has sent a surprise video message to 13-year-old Zaher praising his courage and inviting him to spend the day together at a Real Madrid game.

Zaher lost both his legs after a drone strike in Khartoum, Sudan, where the battle between Sudan's army and the RSF continues to devastate the country.

When the BBC first met him in 2025 he said that he dreamt of being able to walk and play football again. His story resonated with viewers and money was raised for treatment in Cairo, including prosthetic legs.

After surgery followed by months of physiotherapy and psychological support in Cairo, Zehar returned to Sudan feeling "uplifted" by Vini Jr's message he says.

Read more here.

News.title: Temperatures to dip to -5C as first cold health alerts of season issued
News.content:
The first cold health alerts of the season have been issued for parts of England as a blast of Arctic air is set to sweep into the UK.

From midweek onward, overnight temperatures in many towns and cities will fall below zero, bringing the most widespread frost of the season so far.

Some rural spots could see overnight temperatures as low as minus 5C or lower.

Sleet and snow will be possible in some far northern locations with strong wind gusts causing bitter conditions.

News.title: US Army soldier suspected of spying for Russia arrested in UK
News.content:
A soldier in the US Army has been arrested on suspicion of spying for Russia, British counter-terror police have said.

The 41-year-old senior serviceman was arrested near Gloucester on Tuesday.

Counter Terrorism Policing London said the man had been arrested under section one and section three of the National Security Act 2023.

Section one of the Act relates to obtaining or disclosing protected information, while section three relates to assisting a foreign intelligence service.

As part of the investigation, officers are carrying out searches at two locations in Gloucestershire.

The BBC understands the soldier was based at Imjin Barracks in Innsworth, Gloucestershire. The barracks serve as the headquarters of Nato's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps (ARRC), a strategic operational base for the alliance.

Counter Terrorism Policing said it was not linked to any other ongoing investigations.

FBI director Kash Patel said in a statement: "This important arrest involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies."

He added: "While this investigation is continuing, I want to send a clear message â this FBI has no tolerance for anyone who breaks their oath to the United States and whose actions endanger our national security and that of our partners."

News.title: London borough is Britain's happiest, survey finds
News.content:
Richmond upon Thames has been named as the happiest place to live in Britain in an annual survey.

Residents of the south-west London borough have easy access to central London and strolls along the Thames on their doorstep, as well as boutiques, cafes and opportunities to spot roaming deer in their local parks.

Richmond ranked particularly highly across several aspects of local life in Rightmove's "happy at home index", including access to nature and green spaces, essential local services, shops and restaurants, employment opportunities as well as residents' pride in their area.

But, living there comes at a cost, with the average asking price for a home in the borough standing at more than Â£1m.

Harrogate in North Yorkshire and Cirencester in Gloucestershire came in second and third places respectively in Rightmove's 15th annual "happy at home index".

In Wales, Monmouth was the highest ranked, while Kirkcaldy took the top spot for Scotland.

News.title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off
News.content:
"In the main, our mission is to sell to our farmers. We are keen that wherever possible we can achieve that continuity," Morris explained.

"For many of our farmers, it's a generational aspiration to own their farm. A few people have said it to me: 'My grandfather wanted to buy his farm. My father wanted to buy the farm. And now I've got the opportunity and it's an amazing outcome'.

"That's kind of what's driving me through what, at times, has been a little bit of turbulence."

The Duchy - which was established in 1337 - currently has around 700 agricultural lettings, with around 300 whole farm holdings made up of a farmhouse, land and buildings.

Farmers are on a mix of contracts ranging from time-limited to lifelong, with an option to pass the tenancy down through a family.

George Dunn, TFA chief executive, said the organisation was in "deep discussions" with the Duchy and that poor communication had led to tenants "facing prolonged uncertainty over valuations, timing and the options available to them".

"Once a family is told that its long-term relationship with the Duchy may change permanently, that uncertainty lives with them 24/7," he told the BBC.
