He added that while he welcomed the Duchy's assurance that "nobody will be made homeless" not every tenant "will be able or want to buy the farms that they operate and fair alternatives must be explored for those for whom ownership is unaffordable".

A spokeswoman for the Duchy said: "We are engaging with people directly and supporting them through the process with care and respect.

"We recognise that each of our tenant's circumstances are different, and we are taking a careful, case-by-case approach."

News.title: Bid to restore rare Atlantic rainforest secures £6m lottery grant
News.content:
Almost Â£6m has been given to a five-year project set up to restore Scotland's rare rainforest.

The award from the National Lottery Heritage Fund will support the creation of three hubs to be located in Torridon, Morvern and mid-Argyll.

Through the Our Rainforest Futures project local people will be given training and work opportunities around habitat restoration, deer management and the removal of invasive species.

About 75,000 acres (30,351ha) of rain-soaked woodlands on the west coast are designated Atlantic rainforest because of the rare oceanic plant life.

News.title: New photos are 'essential evidence' of possible SAS war crimes, inquiry told
News.content:
An inquiry into UK special forces operations in Afghanistan has released photos described as "essential evidence", showing soldiers could have executed unarmed people lying asleep.

For the first time, the inquiry has made public photos taken of the deceased, across two SAS operations, that show multiple individuals lying in bed with shots to the head.

The inquiry's lead barrister, Oliver Glasgow KC, said the photos may be evidence of possible war crimes and worthy of expert interrogation.

The public inquiry is examining allegations that the SAS murdered unarmed civilians and detainees on night raids between 2010 and 2013 and planted weapons to cover up the killings.

The graphic photographs show multiple unarmed people lying in bed.

One person was tucked under a floral blanket, others with their heads on pillows, blood pooling around their heads. Blood spatter is visible low on the wall in one of the images, consistent with someone being shot while lying down.

Glasgow described how many "look like they sustained head shots" and in a number of cases "there appears to be a dead body with his head on a pillow".

He said further analysis may be able to confirm if the people in the photographs were "shot when asleep".

Seventeen people were killed across the two operations which took place in Helmand province in 2011. The youngest of those killed in each of the operations were 15 and 14 years old respectively.

Glasgow said the photos appeared to contradict the accounts given by the SAS and would have raised serious questions for the military police officers investigating the operations as potential murders.

Lt Col John Harvey, who led the military police's murder probe, agreed they "didn't look right".

He told the inquiry his team were clear the photos could be vital evidence.

Despite the repeated requests of the police investigators to submit the photographs for further testing, this never took place.

One of the investigators, speaking on the condition of anonymity, told the BBC "you can see why we were concerned", adding: "Bullet marks on the walls so low to the ground appeared to undermine the special forces' version of events."

The inquiry is subjecting the photographs to expert forensic analysis.

BBC Panorama has been investigating allegations the SAS executed unarmed civilians and children for more than eight years. The public inquiry was established in 2022 in the wake of Panorama's revelations.

The photos appear to support the findings of Panorama's 2022 investigation into raids in Helmand province which took place a decade before.

Panorama travelled to Afghanistan to gather evidence related to four raids on homes that killed 26 people.

The BBC visited the same guesthouses where the photographs released by the inquiry on Tuesday were taken. Panorama's team were the first British investigators to visit the sites of the shootings, despite a five-year-long military police investigation.

Official special forces accounts of the incidents claim Taliban insurgents opened fire on troops as they entered the compounds, forcing the SAS to return fire and kill those inside.

However weaponry experts told the BBC evidence collected by Panorama indicated multiple rounds appeared to have been fired from above.

This suggests those killed were either lying down or sitting against the wall and not in a firefight.

Family members also told Panorama those killed had been shot cleanly in the head or chest - a common characteristic of a deliberate SAS shooting at close range.

The photographs released by the inquiry show multiple "traumatic injuries to the head or face" of those killed by the SAS, according to its lead barrister.

The inquiry also heard evidence that calls into question whether alleged war crimes were thoroughly investigated.

It heard how investigators were still in Afghanistan in July 2019 gathering evidence as senior officers prepared to close their murder investigation and inform ministers.

The military police investigators were looking for eyewitnesses to unlawful killings and the planting of weapons.

One member of the Afghan partner unit that served on operations alongside the SAS told military police he had personally witnessed a British soldier planting a rifle on an unarmed person after they had been killed.

News.title: Tonnes of dumped rubbish leaves £10m business park an 'apocalyptic' mess
News.content:
An empty multi-million pound business park looks like "an apocalypse" after tonnes of rubbish and a caravan was dumped on the site by people living there.

Brocastle Business Park in Bridgend was built in 2021 with Â£10m from the Welsh government, but locals said about 100 people living in 40 caravans were there for several months.

The park, which has sat empty for five years, has rubble, garden waste, black bags and an old caravan strewn across the vast site.

"It felt like an apocalypse was happening," said the owner of a nearby beauty shop.

The Welsh government said it was an unauthorised occupation and fly-tipping was a crime, adding that steps to remove the waste were under way.

News.title: Train attack driver's '10 seconds' to change line
News.content:
The driver of a high-speed train where a mass stabbing took place said he had "probably about 10 seconds" to decide to switch to the slow line before making an unscheduled stop.

Andrew Johnson was driving the London-bound LNER service on 1 November last year when the train stopped at Huntingdon in Cambridgeshire.

Giving evidence, Johnson told jurors at Cambridge Crown Court he heard someone on the intercom "screaming 'there's a knifeman stabbing people'".

Anthony Williams, 33, of Peterborough, denies 10 counts of attempted murder on the train.

He is also charged with four other attempted murders following earlier incidents in Peterborough and London.

News.title: The Monaco summit that will decide the future of Carrick and Man Utd
News.content:
Michael Carrick's future as Manchester United head coach will be determined 800 miles away from Old Trafford in Monaco on Wednesday.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are flying out for one of their regular pre-planned meetings to discuss strategy around the football club.

On this occasion, the main issue to be decided is Carrick's future and what should happen next.

It is expected that Berrada and Wilcox's recommendation is for the head coach to go.

The Red Devils have opened talks with USA head coach Mauricio Pochettino about replacing Carrick, should he be sacked.

It is not a situation Sir Jim Ratcliffe can have expected to find himself in again, less than three years after purchasing a minority stake in United.

On Christmas Eve 2023, his vision was much different.

"Our shared ambition is clear: we all want to see Manchester United back where we belong, at the very top of English, European and world football," he said.

Instead, United are 18th, in the Premier League's relegation zone after winning just one of their first 10 games and none since August. It is their lowest position so far into a top-flight season since 1986-87 when they were 20th.

Ratcliffe has been criticised for many decisions since he bought his 28.94% stake for just over Â£1bn. This is one he really needs to get right.

News.title: This easy household trick could reduce your energy bill by 10%
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

With winter fast approaching, you might find yourself worrying about the cost of your power bill.

However, there is one simple way that you can cut your electricity consumption – and not many people know about it.

‘Phantom energy’ – also known as ‘vampire energy’ – is the energy consumption that stems from leaving electronic devices plugged into sockets.

It encompasses everything from ubiquitous phone chargers and kitchen microwaves to entertainment systems like televisions and gaming consoles.

"This wasted electricity accounts for about 5 per cent to 10 per cent of home energy use, depending on factors like the age of the equipment," explains Alexis Abramson, dean of the Columbia Climate School.

“Phantom energy depends on ... what kind of systems you have and how much they’ve improved over time.”

open image in gallery Microwaves are big culprits for wasted energy ( Getty/iStock )

For example, TVs that are connected to the internet and have smart wake features that allow them to interact with phones and other devices can consume up to 40 watts of energy during the hours of the day that the TV would normally be off, according to Matt Malinowski, director of the buildings programme at the American Council for an Energy-Efficient Economy.

That's almost 40 times as much as a regular television.

“The good news is there have been new, renewed efforts to tackle this,” said Malinowski.

He said advocates and manufacturers have come up with a voluntary agreement seeking to reduce the amount of energy smart televisions use when they're in standby mode.

Phantom energy contributes to climate change because power drawn by unused devices can increase demand for electricity from sources that release planet-warming emissions.

Aidan Charron, associate director of Global Earth Day, said that while the amount may seem small when a person looks at their individual utility bill, the environmental toll of phantom energy is significant when multiplied over homes across the country.

“Just take a little step of unplugging the things that you’re not using,” he said.

“It will save you money and it’ll save emissions in the long run.”

open image in gallery Smart TVs are also big energy wasters ( Getty/iStock )

What you can do

Some of the main culprits when it comes to draining energy are appliances that are constantly connected to electricity, such as those with a clock.

“Do you really need your microwave to tell you the time, or can you unplug your microwave when you’re not using it?” said Charron.

While unplugging devices may seem burdensome, it significantly contributes to reducing emissions.

Charron recommends starting with small steps like unplugging chargers for phones and other devices once the battery is fully charged. The next step is moving to other appliances such as unplugging an unused lamp.

If unplugging sounds too hard, regularly checking your settings and disabling any extra feature you’re not using that could be draining energy help, too. For example, smart televisions often have optional features that can be turned off so the television isn't listening for signals from other devices while in standby mode.

“If you’re not using it, then you’re getting no benefit, yet you’re paying the price and increased the energy use,” said Malinowski.

Individual actions can make a difference

Individuals also tend to take more sustainable actions, such as unplugging devices, once they learn what they can do to decrease their household emissions efficiently.

Those actions could contribute to reducing U.S. emissions by about 20 per cent per year, which equals about 450 tons (408 metric tons) of carbon dioxide, according to Jonathan Gilligan, a professor of earth and environmental science at Vanderbilt University.

The choices individuals take in their daily lives all add up, Gilligan said, mainly because of how much the U.S. population contributes to direct greenhouse gas emissions.

“The question becomes, what can we do to try to address this?” said Gilligan. “Phantom power is one part of this.”

The more individuals decrease their footprint, the more likely it is that others will follow, too, and eventually, those actions may turn to societal norms, according to Gilligan, because individuals don’t want to feel like they’re being irresponsible.

“This is a place where psychologists find that this effect is real. If people see that other people are doing actions to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions, they want to do that,” said Gilligan.

When it comes to daily choices, individuals may think what they’re doing isn’t really making a big difference. But what they tend to overlook is how they influence others around them by choosing to live a more sustainable life.

The impact may be much stronger than a lot of people realize, Gilligan said.

When is Black Friday 2026?

Black Friday officially falls on Friday 27 November 2026, but you can already shop hundreds of early deals. The likes of Sephora, Lookfantastic, PlayStation and have all launched their sales, with more retailers joining them as November progresses. So, while we're still more than two weeks away from the date itself, Black Friday shopping (and the savings that come with it) is well under way.

For those wondering why the date changes each year, Black Friday takes place the day after Thanksgiving in the US, which is always celebrated on the fourth Thursday of November. Whether it's worth waiting until then is another matter. Some of the strongest offers can appear well before the main event, so I'd recommend checking historical prices before deciding whether to buy now or hold out. Lucky for you, this is something myself and IndyBest’s shopping experts usually flag in our guides – so make sure to browse our descriptions in full before heading to the checkout.

When does Black Friday end?

Cyber Monday (30 November) marks the unofficial end of Black Friday each year, although there's technically no forced cut-off for retailers. Some will pull their discounts at 11:59pm that evening, while others will keep the offers running into early December.

Last year, for example, Lookfantastic continued its promotions until 3 December, and several retailers ran extended Cyber Week sales. However, I wouldn't count on every deal sticking around. Popular products can sell out long before the advertised end date and plenty of discounts are only available for a limited time. If you've spotted something at a jaw-droppingly good price, it's worth checking when that particular offer expires rather than relying on the retailer's wider sale dates.

When is Cyber Monday?

Cyber Monday is on 30 November 2026.

Cyber Monday is the online shopping event that follows Black Friday. It takes place on the Monday after Thanksgiving weekend in the US. It was originally created to encourage shoppers to buy online. But given that everyone shops on the internet, the concept of Cyber Monday is slightly redundant. It’s now just an extension of Black Friday, giving you a final chance to save before Christmas.

Some brands and retailers have tried to popularise other shopping events, but most have had about as much success as Gretchen Wieners trying to make “fetch” happen. There’s Travel Tuesday, for example, which takes place on the day after Cyber Monday and focuses on deals for flights, hotels and package holidays, and Small Business Saturday, which encourages shoppers to support independent retailers instead of the big chains.

How can I tell if a Black Friday deal is genuine?

The easiest way is to check a product’s price history. If it’s been the same price for weeks before Black Friday, or the discount is only a few pounds, it probably isn’t as impressive as it looks. Make sure to write a list of everything you want and need, noting down the current price so you can check the discount in November. I also recommend comparing prices across multiple retailers. Just because something has a big percentage off doesn’t automatically make it a good deal. Having covered sales for more than a decade, I’ve written a detailed guide to my top shopping tips for Black Friday.

Veterans Day is approaching, meaning Americans will see changes in bank hours and mail delivery next week.

No matter the day of the week, November 11 is observed as a federal holiday each year to mark the day in 1918 when troops stopped fighting in World War I.

Originally called Armistice Day when Congress declared the holiday in 1938, Veterans Day honors all veterans, both living and dead, who served in the U.S. Armed Forces.

Government offices, banks and post offices across the country are closed on the holiday, which falls on a Wednesday this year. Depending on the location, many public and private schools stay open, while some restaurants and stores offer deals and discounts for veterans.

Veterans Day is one of 11 federal holidays observed this year.

News.title: Senior doctors strike paused following fresh government talks
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A planned strike by consultant doctors in England later this month has been paused following meetings with the government, the BMA announced.

Consultants in England were set to strike on 25 and 26 November for consultants after the union accused the government of “ignoring concerns” around the “wellbeing and workload” of medics.

This has now been paused to allow for formal negotiations with the government, the union said.

BMA consultants committee co-chairs Dr Helen Neary and Dr Shanu Datta said: “We welcome the opportunity to enter formal negotiations with the Government and hope this marks a turning point in a dispute that has gone on for far too long.

“We’ve always said strikes do not need to go ahead as long as the government is willing to genuinely negotiate, and now is their chance to do so.

“We have received assurances that there are no constraints on what we discuss in these negotiations, and we look forward to hearing their proposals on both pay and working conditions.”

Senior doctors were set to strike on November 25 and 26 in a dispute over pay and working conditions ( PA )

But the BMA warned that “patience is not infinite” and further strikes will be announced if talks fail.

Dr Neary and Dr Datta said: “Consultants have lost a quarter of their pay in real terms over 17 years, while working under increasingly unsustainable pressures.

“But this is about more than pay; it is also about ensuring consultants have the time, recognition and support they need to deliver the best possible care for patients and secure the future of the NHS, while not driving themselves to burn out.

“Pausing strike action in England gives both sides the opportunity to make progress. After 18 months of dispute, however, our patience is not infinite, and should these negotiations fail to swiftly deliver on the issues at the heart of this dispute, we will call further action.

“Consultants deserve a deal that recognises our value and gives us a sustainable future in the NHS, both for ourselves and our patients.”

The government had said in its evidence to the Review Body on Doctors' and Dentists' Remuneration in October that its plan for a 2.4% pay rise for 2027/2028 would not require trade-offs against its health commitments.

The BMA says consultants have seen their pay cut by 25% in real terms over the last 17 years.

A man has appeared in court accused of manslaughter and controlling behaviour following the death of a woman who took her own life nearly four years ago.

Jamie Jordan, 35, appeared before Plymouth Magistrates’ Court in connection with the death of Melanie Jordan, 37, in 2022, and spoke only to confirm his name, date of birth and address during the brief hearing.

The manslaughter charge alleges he unlawfully killed Ms Jordan on December 19, 2022.

The second charge alleges he engaged in controlling or coercive behaviour in an intimate or family relationship, between January 14, 2021 and December 17, 2022.

It is said he “repeatedly or continuously engaged in behaviour which was controlling or coercive, namely, emotionally, sexually, and physically controlling behaviour, towards Melanie Jordan, to whom, at the time of the behaviour, you were personally connected in that you were in an intimate relationship, that behaviour having a serious effect on her and you knew or ought to have known that the behaviour would have a serious effect on her”.

Ms Jordan died at Plymouth’s Derriford Hospital on December 19, 2022 after being found unresponsive at a property in the city days earlier.

open image in gallery District Judge Joanna Matson sent the matters to Plymouth Crown Court ( PA )

District Judge Joanna Matson said the manslaughter allegation related to Ms Jordan taking her own life.

Referring to the court’s better case management form, the judge said: “The likely plea at the Crown Court is going to be not guilty, and Mr Jordan denies that there was any controlling behaviour or coercion on his part, and that he was responsible for Ms Jordan’s suicide.

“That’s what the issue would be at the Crown Court.”

The court heard police inquiries were launched as a result of a coronial investigation into Ms Jordan’s death.

Jordan, of Butterdon Walk, Ivybridge, Devon, was released on unconditional bail.

“I’m sending these matters to Plymouth Crown Court and there will be a pre-trial preparation hearing on December 14,” the judge said.

“I am going to grant you unconditional bail.”

If you are experiencing feelings of distress, or are struggling to cope, you can speak to the Samaritans, in confidence, on 116 123 (UK and ROI) or visit the Samaritans website to find details of your nearest branch.

If you are based in the USA, and you or someone you know needs mental health assistance right now, call or text 988, or visit 988lifeline.org to access online chat from the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. This is a free, confidential crisis hotline that is available to everyone 24 hours a day, seven days a week. If you are in another country, you can go to www.befrienders.org to find a helpline near you.

News.title: Seven things you can do to lower your energy bill this winter
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Chancellor John Healey announced in the Autumn budget that about 20 million households across the UK will get a £100 discount on their energy bills this winter.

The “Household Energy Payment” will grant households in council tax bands A to D a one-off automatic rebate directly to their bank accounts in January 2027.

Households can check whether they would be eligible for the £100 energy bill payment using the government’s own postcode checker.

But even so, more than nine million households are heading into winter owing money to their energy supplier or with no credit on their account, according to a poll from price comparison and switching website Uswitch.

The survey found that 43 per cent of bill payers intended to put on extra clothing instead of switching their heating on, while one in 12 planned to reduce spending on food to cover energy costs.

open image in gallery Chancellor John Healey announced in the Budget that about 20 million households across the UK would get a £100 discount on their energy bills this winter ( PA )

The findings followed an increase in Ofgem's energy price cap on 1 October, when it rose by 3.6 per cent to £1,723 for a typical household. Forecasters are currently predicting a further rise of approximately 22 per cent in January.

However, there are several proactive steps you can take ahead of winter to lower your energy bills.

Here are seven things to do now if you are still worried about energy tariffs.

1. Compare tariffs and consider a fixed rate

There are millions of households in the UK on standard variable tariffs (SVT) right now who could save themselves money by switching to a fixed-rate tariff.

Invest at least £100 in Stocks or ETFs of your choice. Get fractional shares worth £50! Terms and conditions apply. Go to website 

Invest at least £100 in Stocks or ETFs of your choice. Get fractional shares worth £50! Terms and conditions apply. Go to website 

“The SVT is an energy supplier’s default tariff, and is subject to the whims of the market,” explains Gareth Kloet, energy expert at Go.Compare. “So if you’ve just moved house, or come off a fixed rate, you’ll be on an SVT.

“The other choices are a tracker tariff, which is a bit like a variable tariff. It might offer you a saving, for example, £50 off compared to the current price cap. Or you can opt for a fixed-rate tariff, which locks in unit prices and standing charges for a set period, typically 12 to 24 months.”

Price comparison sites can also help customers identify better rates by comparing their current tariff against available options.

“Switching to a fixed rate won’t always be the cheapest option as it depends on what you think is going to happen to gas and electricity prices, but the expectation is that it’ll be rising for at least the next quarter, so fixing for 12 months may be sensible,” advise Kloet.

2. Take a meter reading and switch to direct debit

Whether you’re on a smart meter or not, taking regular meter readings will make sure you’re not paying estimated bills and you’ll avoid inaccurate billing when price caps change.

“Submitting a gas meter reading will also stop your supplier from over or under-billing you,” explains Kloet. “You definitely want to submit a meter reading before the next price cap, particularly if you’re not on a fixed-rate tariff.”

He adds that regularly sending readings can help with budgeting.

open image in gallery Ofgem’s energy price cap rose by 3.6 per cent to £1,723 for a typical household on October 1 ( Getty/iStock )

“You might increase your direct debit to pay off future rising bills, or you might be in credit, and want to reduce it,” says Kloet.

In addition, paying your energy bill by direct debit could save you a significant amount of cash a year.

“If you are paying on receipt of a paper bill you will be paying a premium and you should just switch to direct debit to save cash,” advises Kloet.

3. Use smart technology to manage energy use

Smart meters help you save money by providing real-time data and removing guesswork from your energy bills.

“You can check if you have a smart meter by looking for a digital display, otherwise it will have dials,” says Kloet.

“If you do have a smart meter, many energy firms have an app to help you track usage where you can log in, and it will show how much you’re using in a simple graph format.

“A smart energy monitor can also help you track real-time consumption and identify specific appliances that are wasting energy.”

The vast majority of energy customers are on flat-rate tariffs, which means they pay the same unit price regardless of time of day. However, some households can still access the two-rate meter, known as Economy 7.

“Check your energy bill and if it has two meter readings on it, that means you can use the cheaper off-peak rate,” advises Kloet.

4. Optimise boiler and thermostat settings

In most homes, central heating is the most significant household energy expense.

“Keeping your thermostat between the recommended range of 18-21C, turning off heating in unused rooms, setting working radiators between 2-3 on the dials, and adjusting boiler flow temperatures on the boiler can all significantly reduce costs,” Kloet said.

After heating, cooking is the next most expensive.

“Using air fryers or microwaves instead of ovens, switching to LED bulbs, not forgetting your Christmas lights, and avoiding standby power can save money,” highlights Kloet. “Even boiling just the amount of water needed in a kettle can save cash.”

He also recommended closing the curtains as soon as it gets dark.

open image in gallery The Warm Home Discount gives a £150 discount on the electricity bill for those who meet the required benefit and household criteria ( Getty/iStock )

“If you’ve got a radiator under your window, and most people do, and you have Venetian blinds, point the blinds upwards so the heat that’s rising is reflected into the room,” Kloet reccomended.

“Also reflectors behind radiators direct heat back into the room instead of being absorbed into the wall.”

5. Check if you’re eligible for financial support

Beyond the freshly announced £100 Household Energy Payment, the Warm Home Discount gives a £150 discount on the electricity bill for those who meet the required benefit and household criteria.

In England, customers can access the Crisis and Resilience Fund for emergency cash and fuel vouchers.

In Wales, emergency grants are available from the Welsh Government Discretionary Assistance Fund, and the Scottish Welfare Fund in Scotland.

You can check what benefits you’re entitled to on MoneyHelper or on Turn2us benefits calculator.

6. Contact your energy supplier for help

Many people worry about getting into debt with their energy bill, but it’s important nobody puts themselves at risk by turning their heating off, or ignores mounting bills.

“If you’re worried about your energy bill, I can’t over-stress how important it is to speak to your energy supplier. They will do their absolute utmost to help you get back up to date – they don’t just cut people off,” says Kloet.

“Normally they give you a repayment plan that would allow you to recover the debt over the period in which it accrued. And some energy suppliers also have crisis and hardship funds.”

7. Register for extra support if you’re vulnerable

The free nationwide priority services register provides extra support for vulnerable individuals who are of state pension age, with a disability or chronic illness, mental health condition, pregnant or has children under five.

“If there’s any vulnerability in your property, sign up to the priority services register with the utility supplier,” advises Kloet. “While it doesn’t directly lower bills, it means that if anything happens to their supply or help is needed with meter readings, they will be prioritised over somebody who is fit and able.”

News.title: Poundland hopes for more time to secure rescue deal as deadline looms
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Hopes are mounting that Poundland can get more breathing space to hash out a rescue deal as the retailer approaches a deadline to secure a buyer.

The struggling retailer filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators at the end of October.

This gave the business 10 days to secure a potential rescue deal, which will expire at midnight.

It is understood a deal has not yet been reached, but the company is expecting to get an extension which would allow more time, according to sources cited by the BBC.

It is understood that Poundland’s owners have enabled the release of around £10 million worth of funding to be used for things such as paying staff, taxes and suppliers of stock.

Any extension to Wednesday’s deadline could mean the prospect of a deal that would satisfy the company’s creditors remained on the table.

If not, then it is expected that administrators would be appointed – with corporate advisory firm AlixPartners understood to be lined up.

This would pose a threat to the future of its roughly 600 shops and 11,000 employees.

Advisers have been in talks with parties interested in buying the brand or parts of the business such as swathes of shops.

It has held talks with potential bidders including Tesco over proposals to buy up to 150 shops, and other chains such as Iceland and Lidl.

Investment firm Xyra Holdings has emerged as a potential buyer for the entirety of the business, while Irish real estate firm Martin Property Group is believed to remain interested in a deal.

Gordon Brothers previously rejected a takeover offer from Martin Property Group but management named them as their preferred bidder last month.

News.title: Stacy Keach death: Mike Hammer and Prison Break star dies aged 85
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Stacy Keach, one of America's finest stage actors who became best known for playing scruffy private eye Mike Hammer on TV and whose career was nearly derailed after he was imprisoned in 1984 for trying to smuggle cocaine into Britain, died Tuesday. He was 85.

Keach died at home in Magdalenka, Poland, “after a long and difficult battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure,” his wife, Malgosia Tomassi Keach, said in a statement. Keach had previously suffered a heart attack onstage in Chicago in June 2017.

Though he was considered a preeminent interpreter of Shakespeare and a favorite of such legendary directors as John Huston, Keach was indelibly linked with his take on the hard-boiled Hammer, the fictitious TV private detective created by crime novelist Mickey Spillane.

Unwilling to do the same thing over and over, Keach left behind a crazy quilt of roles, playing a stoner cop on film, King Lear onstage and also narrating World's Most Amazing Videos on TV. He played a deranged colonel in The Ninth Configuration (also known as “Twinkle, Twinkle Killer Kane”), led the TV show “Titus” and had a role in Alexander Payne’s Oscar-nominated drama Nebraska. Last year, he had an excellent turn as George Clooney's bitter father in Jay Kelly.

open image in gallery Stacy Keach arrives for a gala screening of his new film "Nebraska" directed by Alexander Payne, at the AFI Fest 2013 ( Reuters )

“My objective was to have as varied a selection of roles as possible. It probably did hurt my career,” he told New York magazine in 2012. “My choices have had a cost attached to it. But I’ve gotten to play Hamlet, and Richard III, and King Lear, and I would not give that up for anything.”

He played French painter Julien Mistral in the CBS miniseries Mistral's Daughter, a Russian prince in the miniseries version of Judith Krantz's novel Princess Daisy, Barabbas in Franco Zeffirelli's Jesus of Nazareth and Maj. Jonas Steele in The Blue and the Gray. He won a Golden Globe playing Ernest Hemingway in a six-hour miniseries, for which he gained 35 pounds (16 kilograms).

Keach earned a Tony Award nomination for his portrayal of Buffalo Bill in the Broadway play Indians, played Edmund opposite Lee J. Cobb in King Lear on Broadway and had other onstage roles there in The Kentucky Cycle in 1993, The Country Wife in 1965 and Other Desert Cities in 2011.

He also headed the national touring company cast of Frost/Nixon, portraying the fallen president, and went on tour with Sleuth with Maxwell Caulfield as his co-star. He starred in a 2006 production of King Lear at the Goodman Theatre in Chicago and returned in 2017 for Pamplona, a one-man show about Hemingway, where he collapsed onstage, leading to the run's cancellation.

While he was still doing Mickey Spillane’s Mike Hammer (later titled “The New Mike Hammer”), Keach was arrested in 1984 at London's Heathrow Airport after trying to smuggle 1.3 ounces of cocaine concealed in an aerosol shaving cream can and elsewhere in his luggage. Also arrested was his secretary.

“As my sentence was read – nine months in prison – I felt like someone had kicked me in the groin with lead cleats,” he wrote in his 2013 book, “All in All: An Actor’s Life On and Off the Stage.” He added: “It was the lowest moment of my life.”

open image in gallery Actor Stacy Keach, from the film "Nebraska," and his wife, Malgosia, (R) arrive at the 86th Academy Awards in Hollywood, California March 2, 2014. ( Reuters )

He was handcuffed and taken to prison, a cell the size of a closet and where an orange plastic bucket would serve as his toilet. Before he went inside, an officer asked him to autograph a copy of the book The Blue and the Gray.

The then-44-year-old actor was sent to Reading Prison, a medium-security lockup, because authorities felt a minimum-security jail would have provided too easy access for reporters. He was released after six months.

In his book, Keach wrote that while in prison he got warm letters from Gregory Peck, Burt Reynolds, Roger Moore and Al Pacino. He was put in charge of showing a movie one Sunday per month and recalls once picking his own, The Long Riders. He said the experience was “very lonely, very depressing, very sad. I spent a lot of my time trying to re-evaluate my own stupidity.”

After prison, he narrated the TV documentary High on the Job, and testified before Congress, telling a House panel how he first became hooked on cocaine in the mid-1970s. “There is no greater imprisonment than that of being dependent on a chemical substance for one's existence,” he testified.

Keach took his warnings to college campuses and rehab centers. He also married Polish actor Malgosia Tomassi, whom he met when she appeared in the Hammer series. He said he treasured her photos and letters behind bars.

Keach, who was married four times, is survived by Malgosia, and his children, Shannon and Karolina.

His first role after his release was in the CBS movie, Intimate Strangers with Teri Garr, and it became the third-highest rated TV movie of the 1985-86 season. His next film, The Return of Mickey Spillane's Mike Hammer, also played well, and then the Mike Hammer series, which had been on the production shelf since his arrest, was given a slot on CBS' 1986-87 schedule.

open image in gallery Stacy Keach at the 2018 Cannes Film Festival ( Reuters )

Many years later, in the TV series Prison Break that aired from 2005-2017, Keach played a prison warden and said he tried to model his character after his real-life warden in England, whom he said had great compassion and wanted to help inmates rehabilitate themselves.

Born in Savannah, Georgia, Keach was the son of actors who met at Northwestern University. Keach attended the University of California, Berkeley, where he earned degrees in English and dramatic art.

In the summer of 1963, he worked with the Oregon Shakespeare Festival and played Henry V, Mercutio and Lord Berowne. He attended the Yale School of Drama and, in the summer of 1964, played several roles at New York’s Public Theater in Hamlet with Julie Harris. He went to study at the London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art as a Fulbright scholar and returned to New York to do various stage roles.

Keach made his film debut in 1968 in The Heart Is a Lonely Hunter and played stoner cop Sergeant Stedenko from the Cheech and Chong movies. He worked for director John Huston twice, in Fat City and The Life and Times of Judge Roy Bean and had roles in American History X with Edward Norton and The Bourne Legacy. He played a tough trucker in Roadgames, was electrocuted in Children of the Corn and a robot removed his heart in Class of 1999.

His biggest break, though, came with the role of Hammer, whom he played as a modern-day knight, a champion of the underdog.

“Keach makes a dashing, dapper Hammer. He looks almost jaunty in his tilted gray fedora,” said Fred Rothenberg, a TV writer for The Associated Press, in 1983. “He knows how to speak lust with his eyes, and talk dirty with his fists.”

News.title: Young women must ensure they are vaccinated as measles cases surge, doctors say
News.content:
But the dangers for pregnant women, say experts, are often ignored.

There has been relatively little data on maternal and infant measles deaths related to pregnancy in the West since the late 1960s, after the MMR vaccine was introduced and case numbers fell significantly.

Pregnant women are known, however, to be much more vulnerable to illness from measles than others, as the mother’s body, to stop it from rejecting the pregnancy, shifts its immune response significantly and becomes more susceptible to disease.

Between 2000 and 2025, 36 children and adults died from measles or related infections in England and Wales, according to NHS data, but whether or not any of those people were pregnant has not been made public.

“Given the recurrence of measles outbreaks and the number of cases occurring in adults, there may be value in better understanding the impact of measles infection during pregnancy in the UK,” Kirsty Le Doare, professor of vaccinology and immunology at City St George’s, told The Telegraph.

One study by the US CDC conducted in Namibia looked at 55 unvaccinated women who contracted measles during their pregnancies.

Of them, 53 required hospitalisation for complications arising from the virus, ranging from severe diarrhoea, pneumonia, and encephalitis (swelling of the brain).

Another meta-analysis, published in The Lancet in 2018, analysed data from 19 academic papers from countries including France, Germany, and the UK that had studied pregnancy-related measles between 1941 and 2012.

Of 420 pregnancy-related measles cases, 18 deaths occurred, mostly from pneumonia.

“Measles in pregnancy is serious and can cause stillbirth, premature labour and miscarriage,” the NHS website reads. “There is no medical treatment for measles; MMR vaccination is the best protection against becoming seriously unwell,” it adds.

“We know that if you catch measles during pregnancy, you are very likely to end up in hospital,” Professor Helen Bedford, a professor of children’s health at Great Ormond Street Hospital, told The Telegraph.

“You are much more likely to have pneumonia, and there are higher rates of encephalitis. These are all complications that can happen in adults with measles, but they do seem to occur at much higher rates during pregnancy,” said Prof Bedford.

News.title: Gaza floods are an “immediate humanitarian emergency”, warns Trump’s Board of Peace
News.content:
Donald Trump’s Board of Peace has accused Israel of an “insufficient” response to deadly floods that have hit the Gaza Strip.

In a rare statement, the US-led body, charged with ending war in Gaza and rebuilding the Strip, called on Israel “to act immediately to authorise and facilitate the entry of all necessary winterisation and humanitarian supplies”.

“The situation no longer represents simply a threat posed by the approaching winter, but an immediate humanitarian emergency,” they said on Monday.

The Board has been pushing Israel for at least a month to speed up its “winterisation” policies so that residents in Gaza are better able to withstand the coldest months of the year.

The statement followed a weekend of torrential rain and winds that battered the decimated territory’s displacement camps, causing widespread flooding, landslides and several deaths.

A mother and her three young children were killed when a sand dune collapsed onto their tent in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza. The children, aged four, five and eight died on Sunday. Their mother also suffocated under the sand.

News.title: Fears over Ebola spread in DRC as patients flee attack on treatment centre
News.content:
A statement from the health body said: “Health facilities have been attacked and patients, including hundreds people with confirmed or suspected Ebola infection, have fled in search of safety raise serious public health concerns.



“In an Ebola outbreak, every interruption to patient care, contact tracing and disease surveillance creates additional risks for communities already facing extraordinary hardship.



“People must be able to seek treatment safely, and health workers must be able to deliver essential services without fear of violence.”



The body called for a “corridor of peace, protection of civilians, patients, health workers and health facilities, and for safe, sustained access to affected communities”.



The ADF is one of the most feared of scores of armed militia operating in eastern DRC.



The group was originally formed in Uganda in the 1990s by people accusing the government of persecuting Muslims. The army routed the group and the remnants fled across the border, starting a campaign of terror in DRC, before swearing allegiance to IS in late 2018.



The group has since become notorious for its bloody attacks on civilians, which human rights groups say have amounted to war crimes or crimes against humanity.



Earlier this year, Amnesty International, said that advances by the separate Rwanda-backed March 23 movement (M23) militant group in the same region had left Congolese forces overstretched. The ADF had been able to increase attacks in the resulting security vacuum.



The charity said the great majority of victims were Congolese Christians, but the ADF also kills local Muslims who disagree with their interpretation of Islam.



Officials said the attackers struck the village about 30 miles west of Beni around 11 pm local time ‌on Thursday, officials said.



The medical director of the Kelele hospital, Dr Christian Kakule Vulembera, told Radio Okapi, a UN-backed radio station: “Around midnight, the hospital emptied of its patients. All the patients left, including those who were in isolation for suspected Ebola virus infection.”

Attempts to curb the Ebola outbreak have been undermined by suspicion and poor security, with local people frequently turning on health workers.



Conspiracy theories are rife that the outbreak is a hoax to enrich aid agencies, or alternatively that health workers are spreading the disease for their own ends.



Doctors Without Borders, the medical aid charity, over the weekend condemned an attempted arson attack targeting an Ebola treatment centre in Biautu, Beni, North Kivu, where 36 patients were hospitalised.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Man Utd are in relegation trouble and Carrick must be sacked
News.content:
Michael Carrick says he has been given no assurances about his future beyond this afternoon’s crucial game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford.



United are searching for only their second Premier League win of the season and first in 70 days after the club’s worst start to a campaign for 40 years piled the pressure on Carrick.



They dropped into the relegation zone last night following Nottingham Forest’s victory over Manchester City and will be bottom by the end of the weekend if they lose to Villa and Crystal Palace and Sunderland both win.



The Old Trafford hierarchy opted to give Carrick more time to try to turn their season around following a 3-0 hammering by Bournemouth and 4-1 drubbing in Como, since when United have been beaten 2-0 by Chelsea and recovered from two goals down to overcome Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday night.



Asked if he had been told outright he would still be in charge next week, Carrick said: “No - no. Just carry on as absolute normal.”



Pressed on when he felt his future was uncertain, the head coach added: “No, no. Whatever happens and what’s going to happen is going to happen in terms of the game, we’ve got to prepare right.



“I’m really looking forward to playing at home on the back of the other night. The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming and energised and feeling good about what they might see and we’ve got to repay that.”



Another defeat would leave the United board with a big decision to make around Carrick’s future at a time when they are under severe attack from the fanbase.



United’s game against Roma was briefly interrupted when tennis balls were thrown on to the pitch in the first half of a game notable for more furious protests against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.



Three people were arrested by Greater Manchester Police for throwing items on to the pitch and are understood to have been hit with automatic three-year football banning orders as a consequence.



More in-stadium demonstrations are expected today with regular match going fans encouraged not to buy alcohol or drinks inside Old Trafford and again release green and gold balloons before kick-off.



Green and gold were the club’s original colours as Newton Heath and have become a symbol of protest against the ownership.



Asked why there had been such a big drop-off from last season, Carrick added: “It’s just inconsistency, that’s within games,” he said.



“It can be a number of things, it’s never just one thing: a bit of decision-making, a bit of concentration, things going against us in certain points, sometimes we haven’t helped ourselves. So there’s no excuses for it, it is what it is. The great thing is we can do something about it.”

News.title: Energised England deliver statement win to take heat off Borthwick
News.content:
England’s players delivered on their self-created ultimatum to “do it for Steve” by annihilating an abysmal Australia. Barring an extraordinary sequence of events, Borthwick will now remain as head coach through to the World Cup.

Even if Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney’s vote of confidence in the head coach last week was delivered without caveats, he would still have been forced to play the role of reluctant Caesar if the crowd turned mutinous, as they did four years ago. That resulted in Sweeney delivering the thumbs down on Eddie Jones’s reign.

Yet this did not come to pass, as England showed plenty of fire and fury on behalf of their head coach after his control of the dressing room was questioned last week. With 14 minutes to go the crowd, who had been muted on Remembrance Sunday, broke into a rendition of Swing Low, indicating their own approval.

It was not perfect. Attack coach Lee Blackett will be hugely frustrated that they only scored seven tries from a staggering 22 entries into the Australia 22. They also took their foot off the Wallabies’ throats in the final quarter, although they did surpass their highest points total against the visitors. Probably the biggest disappointment was the injuries suffered by wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and centre Seb Atkinson, who had both enjoyed strong games until that point.

News.title: Lando Norris wins chaotic Sao Paulo Grand Prix but F1 season is fizzling out
News.content:
Lando Norris will start today’s Sao Paulo Grand Prix on pole position after a chaotic qualifying session at Interlagos yesterday. A red flag was thrown a matter of moments into qualifying, which led to a lengthy delay of around an hour and a half. When racing did resume, the conditions were treacherous but it was the 2025 world champion Norris who coped best by claiming his third straight pole at Interlagos.

“It has been a long day,” Norris said after taking pole. “It has been a great qualifying. To be on pole again here, two years in a row, different conditions to last year, but I am very happy. It is not easy conditions out there, especially when you know it is going to rain a lot more. It was about getting two laps in at the beginning, not making any mistakes, and that is exactly what we did, so it has been a very good day.

“This was my first time driving the car in the wet, so I think I figured it out pretty quick. It is tough because you are wet, intermediates, all different tyres, and it was very windy the last couple of laps. It was certainly a good day for learning for me and good to take into tomorrow [today]. These guys [Mercedes] are also very quick. Just happy. Today [yesterday] is about getting on pole. It does not really matter how you do it, so very pleased with that.”

News.title: Chelsea bullied by Brian Brobbey and Sunderland
News.content:
Today is must-win match: for both sides.

For Sunderland that argument is easy to make – they are bottom of the Premier League, are without a win since August and for morale, if nothing else need at least a point, though three is really what the doctor orders.

For Chelsea – fourth in the table and with three wins in their past four league outings – the argument that this is a must-win game is harder to make, but bear with me here...

Facing a Sunderland team who are suffering from the worst of both worlds – blunt in attack and pitiful in defence (what a difference from last season...) and have proven all too easy to beat (as their 2-0 home defeat Zagreb illustrated on Thursday) – the west Londoners are expected to win. Fail to return to the capital with the three points and there will once again be question marks over Xabi Alonso’s side. They are flaky and flashy in equal measure, able to play and win well in spurts, but once again unable to mount sustained pressure needed for a title challenge and forced to battle it out for the hope of a top-four spot at best. Those will be the arguments raised should they not win this afternoon.

The hosts doubtless wish that their ‘issues’ were as golden as today’s opposition. For Trai Hume, who scored in this fixture last season, the Sunderland players are at fault for the sorry start to the season and he wants to put right the wrongs so far, starting today.

“I couldn’t tell you what’s changed. We thought we’d addressed it after the Leeds game, where we were aggressive, strong, but we go out there tonight and see the old habits of the start of the season. Everything’s a bit laboured, and it’s something the staff can’t fix, it’s on us as players,” Hume said.

“We’re still together as a club, as a team. I think the run of form we’re on, it would be easy to think we’re not, but we are. We are really upset with how we’ve been playing, and the results don’t lie. We haven’t been good enough and we know that. We have to address that.”

Stay here for all the team news, build-up and action.

Sports.title: Liverpool should have had penalty in 1-0 defeat to Arsenal as Premier League reveal VAR failed to intervene
Sports.content:
Next

LIVERPOOL should have had a penalty for the pull on Alexander Isak’s shirt by Arsenal defender Jurrien Timber, according to a Premier League review.

The Key Match Incidents Panel has ruled VAR Stuart Attwell should have advised on-field referee Andy Madley to award a spot-kick in the November 1 game at Anfield which Liverpool lost 1-0.



With Arsenal ahead through a Kai Havertz goal, Timber tugged on Isak’s jersey as the Reds striker tried to meet a 21st-minute cross from Bradley Barcola.

The KMI Panel agreed by a majority of 4:1 that the offence merited a penalty.



And the five-person review group voted three to two that Attwell should have intervened and asked Madley to look again at the incident after he failed to point to the spot.

But Attwell and his VAR team looked at the incident and cleared it.

Former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard described Attwell’s decision as “an absolute embarrassment”.

Gerrard told The Overlap podcast: “The speed of the cross and how it happened and the reaction, you can understand how a referee could possibly miss that or think there’s not much in that.

“But for someone to sit in [the VAR room] with all these screens around – how you miss that in the VAR seat is an absolute embarrassment.

“To hold someone’s shirt for that long and have three or four opportunities to see that and slow it down, and the amount of cameras that are in stadia at the moment, it’s really poor from Stuart Attwell.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Some observers, including former Liverpool striker Daniel Sturridge and fellow pundit Gary Neville, said Isak should have made more of the incident and would probably have been rewarded with a penalty if he had.

But ex Red Jamie Carragher and former Arsenal striker Ian Wright disagreed.

The KMI panellist who thought Timber’s tug was not an offence believed the “short-lived holding to lack clear impact on the ability of Isak to progress”.

For the same reason – the subjectivity of how much the pull impeded Isak – two panellists said VAR was right not to intervene.

Nevertheless the majority opinion was Liverpool should have had the chance to level the score from the penalty spot in the big match against the PL leaders.



Reds manager Andoni Iraola said the officials’ failure to award a spotkick would lead to players going to ground to make sure fouls were noticed.

The Kop boss told BBC Match of the Day: “There is a clear grab of the shirt.

“Alex was just in front of him. He was going to head in front of the goal, but couldn’t because he grabbed the shirt.



“If he goes to the floor, they call the penalty, 100%. It should be like this, but it is what it is.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Next time, the managers should tell Alex to go to the floor, otherwise they won’t call it.

“The answer is you have to dive. If you don’t dive they won’t call it.”

Sports.title: Martin Zubimendi responds to Arsenal exit rumours as Atletico Madrid and Chelsea linked to January transfer
Sports.content:
Next

MARTIN ZUBIMENDI has rubbished reports that he is close to sealing a January exit from Arsenal.

Zubimendi, 27, has been linked with a move away from North London after struggling for regular game time this season.



The midfielder made 57 appearances across all competitions last season, following his £51m arrival from Real Sociedad in the summer.

But he has fallen down the pecking order under Mikel Arteta this term and is yet to start a Premier League fixture.



Reports in Spain had suggested that Atletico Madrid are close to sealing a January move for Zubimendi, while Chelsea have also been linked with a winter switch.

However, Zubimendi has poured cold water over the rumours in an interview with Spanish outlet Marca.

He said: “To be honest, I’m sometimes surprised by the press.

“I understand that the winter transfer window is approaching and rumors can surface, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish.

“Ultimately, everyone has a team they play for, and we need to respect that. I’ve also read that I might be close, but not at all.

“Often a news story comes out and it seems that if it doesn’t come true, it’s quickly forgotten and nothing happens.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“I’m learning how this world works and getting used to it, but sometimes I could avoid a lot of the messages I receive because of this kind of news.”

Asked if he would like to remain at Arsenal until the summer, at least, Zubimendi added: “Yes, I hope so. I’m happy there.”

SunSport understands that there is interest in Zubimendi from a number of different clubs, given his lack of game time, but no deal is close.

Arteta forked out a whopping £75m on signing Bruno Guimaraes this summer, who – alongside Myles Lewis-Skelly – has been preferred over Zubimendi so far this season.

Despite a lack of minutes, Zubimendi is understanding of how his role has changed after holding talks with Arsenal boss Arteta ahead of the campaign.



The World Cup winner said: “I spoke with Mikel at the beginning of the season. As he does with all the players, he explained the plan to me.

“He warned me that there were new signings and that there would be playing time for everyone. And here we are, fighting for it.

“I understand because, for me, we’re among the five best teams in Europe.

“There are some fantastic players. New signings have arrived in my position, and there were already some very good players.

“I’m also part of that competition that makes it so difficult to get playing time.”



Away from the Premier League, Zubimendi has managed just two starts in the League Cup and one in the Champions League.

However, he has insisted he is happy with how he is handling the situation.

He said: “I’m calm and happy with how I’m handling this situation. It’s something I’ve never experienced before, and I think you learn from these situations too.



“Besides, it’s in moments like these that you need the people around you the most, and they’re there for you.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I’m patient. When you’ve been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to not playing as much, I’m able to see the positive side.

“I think everything passes, that just like last year the opposite happened to me and I played practically everything, this can change very quickly.”

Sports.title: Tense moment Ashley Young confronts Mark Goldbridge over his brutal rant about his Man Utd exit
Sports.content:
Next

ASHLEY YOUNG has confronted Mark Goldbridge over his controversial rant about the ex-Manchester United’s exit from Old Trafford in 2020.

The former England star spent nine years with United and made 261 appearances for the club.



But he decided to join Serie A club Inter Milan midway through the 2019-20 season after losing his place in the team to Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

At the time, YouTuber Goldbridge – who runs the United Stand channel – slammed Young and accused him of leaving the team “a man down” during an injury crisis.



But Goldbridge was left red-faced after Young brought up his comments while the pair appeared on The Overlap’s Stick To United podcast.

Young approached Goldbridge in the studio sand said: “I was gonna get your take on me leaving under Ole [Gunnar Solskjaer].”



He then read out Goldbridge’s post on X at the time, which said: “There’ll be no reaction to Ashley Young leaving United because I don’t care.

“He’s just a modern footballer looking after his own needs and leaving our club and manager a man down when they didn’t want to be. Glad he’s gone but he’s let Ole Gunnar Solskjaer down.”

Goldbridge clarified the post and he replied: “I do vaguely remember it. When did you go? Was it half way through the season?

“Were we having a bit of an injury crisis? I probably looked at it and went ‘he’s going at a time when he needed him to stay’.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Young defended his decision to leave United despite their injury crisis and insisted ex-boss Ole Gunnar Solskjaer had told him he down the pecking order.

He added that Serie A league leaders Inter had told him he would get minutes while also offering Champions League football.

And he said United offered him a new deal but only after they had agreed to let him go – at which point it was too late.

He told Goldbridge: “Ok. My take on it – what actually happened was I went and spoke to Ole.



“Aaron Wan Bissaka was playing and he said to me, ‘you’re not going to play much’. I was 34 at the time and I’m being told Inter Milan are interested.

“I told Ole look I’m not playing and I want to play football. You might have made me club captain but I’ve still got a need. I can’t just sit here and pick up the money.

“The next day he said I’ll let it happen. I was happy. Three days later he said the club want to offer you a new deal. It’s too late. My head was already gone. That was it.

“I can get stick, it’s not a problem. I’ve had it throughout my career. But if it goes personal – my club I’d never leave them.

“If someone said they were in desperate need – Ole didn’t said that. He said you can leave.”



Goldbridge apologised for his harsh words and said it summed up a lack of communication from the club.

He said: “I can take that. Apologies. Also, the communication at that football club, look at the last two weeks with Carrick. No one’s officially said he’s staying.

“I’m sure there’s a lot of players like yourself who go, ‘I can’t believe that’s out there’.”

Young’s old United team-mate Wayne Rooney – who was also featured on the show – chimed in by joking: “I wanna go back and see what you said about me now!”

Young started his career with Watford before signing for Aston Villa and then joining United in 2011.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

He went on to win the 2012-13 Premier League title with the Red Devils in Sir Alex Ferguson‘s last season and also won the FA Cup, Carabao Cup and Europa League.

Young’s last season in English football came with Ipswich Town last season as he helped them win promotion to the Prem.

Sports.title: Legendary talkSPORT host Danny Kelly dies aged 69 as tributes pour in for ‘extraordinary’ presenter
Sports.content:
'WE LOVED YOU' Legendary talkSPORT host Danny Kelly dies aged 69 as tributes pour in for ‘extraordinary’ presenter







Next

MUCH-LOVED talkSPORT host Danny Kelly has died at the age of 69.

Kelly had been part of the radio broadcaster’s coverage since 2007.



But he stepped back in March this year after being diagnosed with throat cancer.

Kelly said in his final appearance: “I’ve learned something really incredibly important in the last few weeks.



“If you feel something just isn’t right in your body, I don’t mean you’ve got a hangnail or a bit of earwax or something, but if you know something is not quite right in your body, for God’s sake, go to the doctor. Get yourself checked out.

“You’ll be hearing me less and less regularly as I concentrate on letting the fabulous medical people do their stuff.

“Thanks for listening to this, which I know hasn’t been easy. Hopefully, with a bit of luck, and the genius of the doctors, we’ll do it all again real soon and long into the future.”

Tributes have been pouring in for Kelly, who fronted talkSPORT’s coverage of Euro 2008 and in recent years was a regular on the show Hawksbee and Jacobs.

Born in London, Kelly spent a large chunk of his career editing music magazines such as NME, before moving into sports broadcasting.

TalkSPORT wrote on X: “We are heartbroken to share that our much-loved friend and colleague Danny Kelly has died, aged 69.



“A cherished part of talkSPORT for so many years, Danny brought extraordinary wit, warmth and knowledge to our airwaves.

“His passion for football, music and life was infectious, and his kindness touched everyone around him.

“We loved you, Danny. We’ll miss you dearly.



“Our thoughts are with Danny’s family, friends and everyone who loved listening to him.”

TalkSPORT’s chief football correspondent, Alex Crook, wrote: “This is so sad. Danny was a great broadcaster and a brilliant colleague and friend.

“Had a wonderful day with him watching Spurs’ last game at White Hart Lane. TalkSPORT will never be quite the same again.”

Reporter and commentator Ian Abrahams posted: “Absolutely heartbroken to hear Danny Kelly has passed away. One of the best broadcasters I’ve worked with.

“One of the most amazing, kindest, funny, passionate people I knew.”



Referencing one of his most famous on-air quotes, Abrahams added: “Danny, we’ll always have ‘I love Football’. I will miss you my friend, sleep well.”

Kelly was a passionate Tottenham fan who featured regularly on The Athletic’s The View From The Lane podcast.

Spurs also mourned his passing, writing: “The entire Tottenham family mourns the loss of one of our own, broadcasting legend Danny Kelly.

“Our thoughts and love are with his family and friends at this incredibly sad time. Rest in peace, Danny.”

And fellow broadcaster Danny Baker, who had worked with Kelly since the early 1990s, wrote an emotional tribute.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

It read: “My great friend, supreme broadcaster and funniest man I ever knew, Danny Kelly, died yesterday afternoon.

“I cannot believe I will never hear his voice again.”

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino’s former agents step in to finalise Manchester United deal with Michael Carrick on brink of sack
Sports.content:
Next

MAURICIO POCHETTINO’S former agents have stepped in to finalise his sensational switch to Manchester United.

Intermediaries approached United over the past week to broker the tactician’s return to English football.



SunSport revealed on Monday that United States boss Pochettino, 54, wants the job as he is eager to return to the Premier League.

Now a deal is being rubber-stamped for him to take over at Old Trafford.



The Argentine still has a home in Hertfordshire from his five-and-a-half-year stint at Tottenham.

He also returned to London to manage Chelsea for one campaign in the 2023/24 season.



And now a move to Manchester, which has been on the cards for the best part of a decade, appears to be edging closer, with several separate parties involved in negotiations.

United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew to Monaco to meet co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to ratify the succession plan.

Wilcox and Berrada are not scheduled to return to Manchester until Wednesday evening, meaning the sacking of Michael Carrick may not be confirmed until Thursday.

Carrick returned to Carrington on Wednesday to oversee first-team training.

MICHAEL CARRICK UPDATES: LATEST ON MAN UTD MANAGER’S FUTURE

Squad members Matthijs de Ligt, Matheus Cunha, Kobbie Mainoo, Tyler Fletcher, Joshua Zirkzee, and Tom Heaton were all present for Tuesday’s workout.

Injured trio Manuel Ugarte, Carlos Baleba, and Benjamin Sesko were also on site on Tuesday, while Marcus Rashford arrived on Wednesday.

Pochettino oversaw US training in Fayetteville, Georgia on Tuesday ahead of their two-legged Concacaf Nations League quarter-final with Haiti.

The US play Haiti in Kingston on Saturday before the return leg in Cincinnati next Tuesday evening.

Pochettino is still scheduled to attend a press conference on Friday and it is unclear whether he will remain in charge of both matches.

Sports.title: Championship striker, 35, juggling £12.5k-a-week football career with second job as financial advisor
Sports.content:
Next

CHARLTON striker Matty Godden has become a fully qualified financial planner.

Despite picking up a reported £12,500 a week at The Valley – which equates to £650,000 a year – the 35-year-old intends to balance his new profession with scoring goals in the Championship.



Godden’s contract runs until the end of the season, with Charlton retaining the option to extend it until the summer of 2028.

But the former Peterborough and Coventry star’s retirement plan is already up and running.



He wrote on a new Instagram profile with IFA (Independent Financial Advisor) on the end of his username: “I’m still enjoying my career as a professional footballer, but now I’m also a fully qualified Financial Planner.

“Football taught me how quickly things can change, and how much it matters to plan ahead.



“Now I help people do just that, whether you’re a professional sportsperson, a family planning for the future, or a business owner looking to make the most of what you’ve built.

“I’ve had a great response so far, with some brilliant meetings booked in for next week.”

Godden already has a profile on the website of Investments & Pensions – a platform offering “impartial guidance – online or face-to-face – to reach your long-term goals”.

Injuries have meant the EFL veteran has only played 104 minutes in the Championship this season, starting once and coming off the bench twice.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But in that short time he managed to notch the winner against Sheffield United in Charlton’s most recent home game on Saturday.

He also netted in August’s Carabao Cup win over Cheltenham.

The Addicks made a nod to Godden’s new job after his late winner against the Blades.

They posted “You’ve been advised by Matty Godden”, complete with his new Linkedin picture.

Sports.title: Man Utd finalising deal for Mauricio Pochettino to become new manager with Michael Carrick set to be sacked
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED are reportedly closing in on a deal to sign Mauricio Pochettino if Michael Carrick is sacked.

The Athletic’s David Ornstein claims that Old Trafford chiefs discussed personal terms with the Argentine tactician‘s representatives on Tuesday with “no issues anticipated.”



United would need to pay £7.4 million to release Pochettino from his USA contract if, as expected, they pull the trigger on Carrick’s departure.

Ornstein’s report suggests that US Soccer have yet to be contacted, with the squad currently preparing for two clashes against Haiti.



Red Devils icon Alex Ferguson has been pushing his former club to sign Pochettino for over a decade and this is the SIXTH time he has been in the frame since a lunch with the Scot in 2016.

Poch admitted previous interest in the role before taking charge of the Stars and Stripes at a home World Cup and suggested after signing a four-year post-tournament extension that he might not see it out.

He said: “Now we are thinking of spending four years with the USA but you can always break a contract, say you stop, and that’s it, you agree something.

“With a four-year contract, it’s different.

“We could lose Copa America or the Gold Cup, and they’re not happy with us, they can sack us, or we can say, ‘OK, it’s not in the way that we think’.”

With a game against fierce rivals Liverpool coming after the international break, United need to make a decision.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew to Monaco to meet co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe while Carrick continues to work at the club’s Carrington training complex.

They have to receive sign-off from Ratcliffe, who then has to OK the decision to part ways with the Glazer family.

SunSport revealed on Monday that Pochettino is open to taking over.



Talks may become complicated, especially when it comes to the rest of his backroom team, and the club risks needing to install a caretaker for the trip to Anfield on November 22.

The first training session for players back from international duty is scheduled for next Thursday.

United are 18th in the table with just one win in 10 Premier League matches and an angry fanbase growing increasingly impatient.

Even if Pochettino is hired, wider questions about the club’s owners, squad and long-term strategy remain.



US billionaire Ken Griffin is emerging as a key figure in the pursuit of the 54-year-old.

Griffin is close to United’s majority owners the Glazers and part-funds Pochettino’s £5m-a-year salary as US team boss.

His Citadel firm own shares in United and helped the Glazers fund their 2005 takeover.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Berrada is believed to be a fan of Pochettino and previously had him on a list of potential replacements for Pep Guardiola during his time at Manchester City.

Eddie Howe, Antonio Conte, Fabian Hurzeler, Unai Emery and Julian Nagelsmann have also been mentioned.

Sports.title: Non-league club put out advert for new MANAGER on X and ask for CVs as they sit rooted to bottom of National League
Sports.content:
Next

NATIONAL LEAGUE side Gateshead have put out an advert for a new manager on social media after sinking to the bottom of the table.

The Tynesiders have just four points from 15 games after just one win and THIRTEEN defeats.



That dismal start saw ex-Sunderland star Lee Cattermole sacked after just four months in charge.

The crisis club are now under new ownership after a American firm agreed a takeover to save them from financial ruin last week.



Gateshead’s future had looked uncertain after failing to pay players and staff their wages for September following director Mark Nellist’s resignation.

And with the new owners in place, the club have taken the unusual step of advertising their manager’s job vacancy on X.



So if you fancy yourself in the dugout, you can send off your application with the click of an email.

Gateshead’s official account put out a post that read: “Gateshead Football Club is seeking applicants for the role of First Team Manager.

“To apply, please send your CV and a cover letter detailing your coaching philosophy and relevant experience to info@gateshead-fc.com.”

The job ad itself said it was looking for a coach to join a “progressive club with strong ambitions both on and off the pitch”.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The requirements for the role was a minimum a Uefa A Licence but “preferably Pro Licence”.

It asked for previous experience in senior football management or as an assistant with “excellent communication and player-management abilities”.

The club are hoping to push on after being taken over by Flacks Group.

The takeover was on the verge of collapse after an issue with third party Shoreline Limited.

But Gateshead are now hopeful for the future after the purchase went through.



Interim chariman Graham Wood said: “Exciting times lie ahead as we learn of Flacks Group’s plans for the club and seek to turn a disappointing start to the season around with the appointment of a new manager.

“Staff and players have now been paid and funds are in place to satisfy HMRC and other creditors.”

Previous owner Nellist had withdrawn his funding at the end of September, which led to their financial crisis as HMRC debts piled up.

Ben Clark is currently in charge of the first team as interim boss.
