Sports.title: Michael Carrick's true feelings about Man Utd sack delay as he's made to take training
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick's true feelings about Man Utd sack delay as he's made to take training

Manchester United are expected to sack Michael Carrick this week - although the Englishman has been taking training as he waits for the axe to fall

View 3 Images Michael Carrick's true feelings have emerged (Image: Getty Images)

Michael Carrick is reportedly growing frustrated at being kept waiting for a decision on his future at Manchester United. The 45-year-old is expected to be formally dismissed this week, with United lining up Mauricio Pochettino as his successor.

‌



‌



News of United's intention to part company with Carrick first emerged on Monday. However, the former Red Devils midfielder is still waiting to be handed his P45 and has continued to oversee training.

‌



According to The Telegraph, Carrick is "resigned to his fate" and has become increasingly irritated by the club's delay in making a formal announcement. It might not be until Thursday that he's informed face-to-face of his sacking.

‌



Carrick took charge of training at United's Carrington base on Tuesday, working with those members of the squad not away on international duty, including Harry Maguire, Mason Mount and Matthijs de Ligt. The 45-year-old was also pictured arriving at the training ground on Wednesday morning and, for now, is expected to remain in charge of sessions.

Man Utd finalising Mauricio Pochettino deal to replace Michael Carrick as manager READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Carrick's sacking is understood to be awaiting final approval following a board meeting in Monaco on Wednesday involving United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox. Berrada and Wilcox reportedly held talks on Monday, when they concluded that a change in the dugout was necessary.

‌



United have maintained that no decision has been made on Carrick's future. However, reports suggest the club want a new head coach in place before their trip to Anfield to face Liverpool on November 22.

Former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino has emerged as the leading contender to take charge at Old Trafford, and a deal to appoint him is reportedly being finalised. The Argentine, who is currently managing the United States national team, is keen on the job.

‌



View 3 Images Michael Carrick has been forced to take training despite reports he is about to be sacked (Image: Getty)

Pochettino signed a contract extension with the USA in August, committing himself to the role until the 2030 World Cup. However, the agreement is understood to contain clauses allowing the 54-year-old to leave for a leading European club if compensation of just under $10million (£7.44m) is paid.

‌



It isn't the first time Pochettino has been in the frame for the United job. He was first linked with a move to Old Trafford in 2016, when he was considered a potential successor to Louis van Gaal. Speculation intensified after he was pictured having lunch with Sir Alex Ferguson, but United eventually turned to Jose Mourinho instead.

Mourinho's departure in December 2018 brought Pochettino back into contention. However, United opted to appoint Ole Gunnar Solskjaer as caretaker manager, with the Norwegian handed the job permanently the following March.

‌



View 3 Images Mauricio Pochettino is in prime position to become the next Manchester United manager (Image: David Berding/Getty Images)

The Argentine's name resurfaced when Solskjaer was dismissed in November 2021. Pochettino was then in charge of Paris Saint-Germain and was reportedly keen to return to the Premier League. However, United turned to Ralf Rangnick on an interim basis before eventually appointing Erik ten Hag as their permanent successor to Solskjaer.

‌



Another managerial vacancy at Old Trafford in 2024 saw Pochettino's name enter the conversation once more. Having left Chelsea by mutual consent, he was among the candidates considered as United weighed up Ten Hag's position following an eighth-place Premier League finish.

Once again, however, United decided against making a move for the Argentine and stuck with Ten Hag. By the time the Dutchman was eventually sacked a few months later, Pochettino had already embarked on a new challenge, taking charge Stateside.

Article continues below

A return to club management would therefore represent another significant turning point in Pochettino's career, with the chance to finally take the reins at Old Trafford, after years of near-misses, potentially within reach.

Sports.title: Man Utd finalising Mauricio Pochettino deal to replace Michael Carrick as manager
Sports.content:
Man Utd finalising Mauricio Pochettino deal to replace Michael Carrick as manager

Manchester United have identified Mauricio Pochettino as their preferred candidate to replace Michael Carrick as manager and have wasted no time in working out the details

View 3 Images Mauricio Pochettino is in prime position to become the next Manchester United boss (Image: David Berding/Getty Images)

Manchester United are working on a deal to make Mauricio Pochettino their next manager.

‌



‌



United chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox are flying out to Monaco for a meeting with Sir Jim Ratcliffe on Wednesday where Michael Carrick's fate will be sealed. Carrick is set to be sacked as manager following a disastrous start to the season, which sees the club 18th in the Premier League.

‌



Berrada and Wilcox have been considering their replacement options since last month, having decided to wait until the international break to make a call. Former Tottenham boss Pochettino is one of the top candidates, alongside ex-Newcastle manager Eddie Howe.

‌



Pochettino has been in the frame for the United job previously and is understood to be very keen on taking over at Old Trafford. The 54-year-old is currently the boss of the United States, having signed a new contract in August after the World Cup.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

But The Athletic reports that the wheels are already in motion for Pochettino to replace Carrick. United chiefs began working on a deal on Tuesday, with personal terms not expected to be an issue.

‌



United will have to pay the United States compensation of $10million (£7.4m), while Pochettino's staff will cost a considerable amount more to release from their deals across the Atlantic.

Pochettino is currently preparing for the USA's Concacaf Nations League quarter-final matches against Haiti. The USMNT play in Jamaica on Saturday before the second leg in Cincinnati on Wednesday.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 3 Images Mauricio Pochettino is currently the head coach of the United States (Image: Robin Alam/Getty Images)

‌



The Argentine has plenty of Premier League experience, having previously taken charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. Despite penning a new contract with the USA until after the 2030 World Cup, he has not tried to hide his desire to return to England.

Pochettino has been interviewed by United on three previous occasions, including most recently in 2024 when the club ultimately decided to stick with Erik ten Hag.

‌



He has been in charge of the United States for two years, having taken over from Gregg Berhalter in September 2024. The former defender has won 21 of 35 matches in charge and his side were knocked out of the World Cup in the last-16 by Belgium in the summer.

View 3 Images Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox are meeting on Wednesday to decide the next steps (Image: Jacob King/Press Association)

United handed Carrick a two-year contract in May after his impressive impact as interim boss following the sacking of Ruben Amorim in January. But the 45-year-old ex-midfielder will be relieved of his duties less than six months later having presided over a miserable start to the campaign.

The Red Devils have won just three of their 15 matches in all competitions, with their points tally of eight from 10 league games representing their worst start in 40 years.

‌



Carrick said he expected to continue as manager after the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday. He was spotted arriving at the club's Carrington training ground on Tuesday as normal, but won't be in charge for their trip to Anfield to play Liverpool on November 22.

Michael Carrick is set to be relieved of his duties as Manchester United manager after a disastrous start to the season left them in the Premier League relegation zone

Michael Carrick is set to be sacked as Manchester United manager in a crunch meeting held in Monaco tomorrow.

The Old Trafford hierarchy are set to finally wield the axe following a disastrous start to the season. United have won just once in the Premier League, leaving them marooned in the relegation zone.

Carrick was given three games to save his job before the international break, but suffered defeat by Chelsea before a stirring comeback saw United beat Roma 3-2.

Sports.title: Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso plotting January transfer swoop for forgotten Arsenal star
Sports.content:
Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso plotting January transfer swoop for forgotten Arsenal star

Chelsea are in the market for Arsenal's Martin Zubimendi, who has fallen down the pecking order, but Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid both believe they can land the Spanish midfielder

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso is looking to raid Arsenal for one of their midfielders

Chelsea are one of three clubs eyeing up a January move for Arsenal's Martin Zubimendi - who is struggling for minutes at the Emirates.

‌



‌



Zubimendi is only into his second year at the Emirates but, after initially being a favourite under Mikel Arteta, the World Cup winner has slipped down the pecking order. As a result his future is the subject of speculation.

‌



The Blues have put the former Real Sociedad midfielder on their radar, but face competition from Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid, reports the Independent. Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso was previously in charge of Real Sociedad B and is known to be a fan of the 27-year-old.

‌



Real were keen on Zubimendi last summer when Alonso was at the helm, but it was ultimately Arsenal who won the race for his signature, securing a £60million deal.

All seven of the Spaniard's Premier League appearances have come off the bench this season, underlining his decline having been a first-team regular last season.

Sports.title: Dominic Calvert-Lewin speaks out on England World Cup snub and new Harry Kane plan
Sports.content:
Dominic Calvert-Lewin speaks out on England World Cup snub and new Harry Kane plan

Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin missed out on a spot in this summer's World Cup squad - but has channelled his disappointment to start the new season in hot form

View 3 Images England and Leeds United striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin

Dominic Calvert-Lewin believes he started this season feeling “refreshed” after his World Cup snub.

‌



‌



Calvert-Lewin admits he was desperate to go to the United States in the summer which would have rounded off a memorable season after helping Leeds stay in the Premier League.

‌



But Calvert-Lewin, 29, insists “everything happens for a reason” and the knock-on effect was that he got some quality time with his family and it is factor as to why he has started this season in good form.

‌



Leeds striker Calvert-Lewin has scored five goals but also wants to stay in the England frame this time feeling that he really deserves it.

‌



Calvert-Lewin said: “Last season, England was obviously in the back of my mind because it’s a by-product of the success you have with your club. But I was so focused on keeping Leeds in the Premier League that I didn’t think too much about anything else.

“Having had the chance to play for England in March, a call up to the World Cup would’ve been an additional bonus. It’s a dream but my mission was accomplished with Leeds. Getting the call was OK.

‌



“I had a nice time with my family and spent a lot of time with my daughter, which was refreshing, and that is why I started this season so well.

View 3 Images Calvert-Lewin has five goals for Leeds this season

‌



“Everything happens for a reason and I’ve got myself back in the fold. The last international break felt like a real call up in comparison to March, so happy to be here.”

Calvert-Lewin is seen as the back-up striker to Harry Kane but he wants to show he can play alongside the newly-crowned Ballon d’Or winner. And he admits everyone now wants to be a striker like Kane after he was crowned the best player in the world.

‌



He added: “When you’re a young kid and watch your heroes play you wanna be like them. There is a high chance of kids wanting to be No 9s going forward. The way he plays is not a traditional No 9 because he can do many different things.

“I’d like to think there are more No 9s and less so players who want to get in the pocket and turn. We’ve got an abundance of those and long may that continues but I like to watch physical No 9s who get in the box and score one-touch finishes.

‌



View 3 Images Calvert-Lewin and England captain Harry Kane

“Harry is someone I’d love to play with. I look at how he likes to get on the ball… he assists as many as he scores so for me I’d be rubbing my hands together.

“Pressure and the pressure of scoring goals is something I embrace. Pressure is a privilege. I embrace it at Leeds, it’s why I play football. I missed the expectation when I wasn’t playing.”

Sports.title: Man Utd draw up fresh plan that could save Michael Carrick ahead of crunch Monaco meeting
Sports.content:
Man Utd draw up fresh plan that could save Michael Carrick ahead of crunch Monaco meeting

Manchester United could still keep Michael Carrick in his role as they seek to further bolster their coaching line-up to ensure the under fire boss has more quality around him

View 2 Images Michael Carrick's future will be decided on Wednesday (Image: OLI SCARFF, AFP via Getty Images)

Manchester United could yet keep Michael Carrick on as boss - but with additional coaching support as the club's senior figures weigh up their next move.

‌



‌



The likes of Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox will sit down at a summit with minority owner and Ineos chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe on Wednesday in Monaco, where the expectation is that Carrick will be removed from his role.

‌



He has presided over a run of one win in 10 Premier League games to start the season, which has left the club in the relegation zone. There has been a willingness to see Carrick succeed and the hierarchy have stood by him despite just three wins all season.

‌



And if Carrick is to remain in charge beyond the international break then there is the option to bring in more coaching quality around him, given the United boss has ultimately never been in charge of a Premier League club.

Bayern Munich coach Aaron Danks, who worked with Carrick at Middlesbrough and was seen as a potential appointment in the summer, is one option, reports the BBC.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Carrick already has Steve Holland alongside him. Holland was previously Chelsea's assistant and then worked as Gareth Southgate's No 2 for a number of successful years with England. But clearly the current set-up is not working and the club are looking to make a positive change.

‌



Ultimately they had never planned for a managerial change, and especially not this early in the season. As a result no one has been lined up and appointing managers midseason presents its own challenges, but there are a number of candidates on their radar, several being out of work.

Mauricio Pochettino is among those who are in a job, he's leading the USA but has been linked with the post previously. Eddie Howe left Newcastle in the summer and could be tempted back into management. His Premier League experience is a plus. Big name foreign coaches are also being eyed, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte are two of the names most regularly mentioned.

‌



View 2 Images Aaron Danks, currently at Bayern Munich, is seen as someone who could come in

Nagelsmann has led Bayern and Germany whilst Conte has won league titles with four different clubs - one of those being Chelsea. Both men who fit the bill of being able to lead a heavyweight club, even if United are at their lowest ebb during the Premier League era.

Article continues below

Carrick's blushes were saved on Sunday when United score twice in stoppage time to draw 4-4 with Aston Villa. United had twice trailed by two goals before making comebacks, but the game continued to showcase their flaws defensively, which have plagued them throughout the campaign.

Pochettino, currently in charge of the USA national team, is being lined up as Carrick's successor with United preparing for a potential parting of ways.

Carrick reported to United's Carrington training ground on Wednesday morning at around 7.45am before it emerged that talks with Pochettino had reached an advanced stage.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Roy Keane says under-pressure Man Utd boss Michael Carrick 'talks a lot but doesn't say much' and needs to 'get moving' on improving the team after watching his former side earn a late 4-4 draw against Aston Villa

While Carrick is in Manchester at the training ground, United's powerbrokers are set to make a final decision on his future at a Monaco summit on Wednesday.

CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox had already been due to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe for a summit to review the club's start to the season.

But with United in the relegation zone after their worst start to a league campaign for 40 years, Carrick's future is increasingly in doubt and expected to be decided at the meeting.

Berrada and Wilcox have to make their recommendation to Ratcliffe, who has control of football operations at Old Trafford, before a final decision is made over Carrick.

Carrick was handed a stay of execution after United's 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth in the Premier League last month, but momentum is now gathering behind a change in the dugout.

Pochettino has long been admired by United, who have held talks with the Argentine on at least two occasions about taking over.

Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United have a well-established history. One where paths might have crossed long before now, numerous times, but somehow never managed to converge.

Sports.title: Super League clubs vote to expand to 15 teams
Sports.content:
The Super League has announced that its 14 clubs have voted in favour of a motion to expand to 15 teams for the 2027 season.

"Super League (Europe) Ltd has today held a shareholders' meeting to determine how many clubs will take part in the competition in 2027," a statement from the league read.

"Having agreed in favour of moving from 14 to 15 clubs, SLE has passed their decision on to the Rugby Football League Board.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player York Valkyrie beat Wigan Warriors in Grand Final to lift Super League title for third time.

"The RFL Board will now set out criteria and assemble a panel to run the process to judge against it.

"A recommendation will be made in due course."

It is understood that clubs will now be invited to apply to be the 15th team in the competition.

London Broncos, who have made no secret of their desire to be in the top flight, completed the treble in 2026 during a brilliant season for them in the Championship.



They are expected to apply to be the next club in Super league. It is not yet known if any other clubs will join the process.



After London went back down to the Championship, they were took over by an ownership group including NRL and Brisbane Broncos legend Darren Lockyer.

Super League clubs approve salary cap amendments

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League Grand Final between Warrington Wolves and Wakefield Trinity.

Clubs also voted in favour of two amendments to the league's salary cap regulations that allow clubs more flexibility with young players and injuries.

The first allows teams to claim salary cap dispensation if a player is injured for over eight cap-relevant matches, allowing clubs to sign a replacement player for the period.

It also forbids teams from claiming further salary cap dispensation should a player who was already exempt from salary cap implications becomes re-injured later in the season, unless he missed a further eight matches which affect the salary cap.

The second allows teams to feature a young player aged 23 and under - who has not previously played in any salary capped games - in two matches without triggering an increase in a club's salary cap spending, with that figure increasing to 50% should they play between three and five matches.

Should the player feature in more than five matches, the full amount of their salary will be applied to the cap.

Sports.title: Cheltenham Festival-winning jockey O'Brien dies
Sports.content:
Two-time Cheltenham Festival-winning jockey Tom O'Brien has passed away at the age of 39 following a lengthy battle with cancer; As a rider, O'Brien notched five Grade One successes before retiring in 2023.

Multiple Grade One-winning jockey Tom O’Brien has died at the age of 39.

O'Brien, who retired from the saddle in April 2023, rose to prominence with trainers Peter Bowen and Philip Hobbs and enjoyed a breakthrough season in 2006/07 with over 100 winners in that campaign.

The first of five Grade One successes came aboard Souffleur for Bowen in the 2007 Challow Novices' Hurdle, while later in his career O'Brien would strike up a memorable partnership with Hobbs' fan favourite Thyme Hill, landing the 2021 Liverpool Hurdle and 2022 Kauto Star Novices' Chase.

O'Brien also rode Dream Alliance to his against-all-odds victory in the 2009 Welsh Grand National, a story which would inspire a Hollywood film called Dream Horse.

Speaking on the Nick Luck Daily Podcast, Johnson White - now co-trainer with Philip Hobbs, said: "You couldn't get a harder working, nicer family man. I messaged Richard Johnson this morning and he sent a message back saying 'life is so cruel' and realistically you can't say any more than that. He leaves a lovely wife Hayley, two wonderful boys and a loving family that were there with him until the end."

British Horseracing Authority (BHA) Chief Executive Brant Dunshea paid tribute, saying: "Tom was held in the highest esteem and meant so much to so many people across our sport, who benefitted from his kindness and loyal friendship.

"He touched countless lives on both sides of the Irish Sea, bringing joy to everyone who had the privilege of knowing him and watching what he did best, on and off the racecourse.

"He will be hugely missed and his loss is immensely difficult to process. The racing family is distraught, but I know how we will all rally round to provide each other with support, comfort and to remember Tom as we knew him best: a brilliant jockey, a valued colleague, a loyal friend and above all a loving husband and devoted father."

Trainer Christian Williams posted on X: "Kind, talented, humble and a true gentleman. Tom was a joy to be around and a privilege to have in the saddle. A friend to so many and of course, always smiling. Our thoughts and prayers are with Hayley, Archie, Toby, their families and many, many friends."

Writing on X, Sky Sports Racing broadcaster Mike Cattermole said: "Really saddened to hear about the passing of Tom O'Brien at 39. Obviously an excellent jockey but just a lovely guy, so gentle and humble. Thinking about all those who were close to him. Life is such a lottery."

Sports.title: Meet the youngest top-flight manager in Europe
Sports.content:
As football has evolved, so have routes into football management.

Once almost exclusively the preserve of former professionals, a playing career is no longer a prerequisite.

That has opened the door to the younger generation. Thirteen managers and head coaches in England's top four divisions are under 40, with Brighton's Fabian Hurzeler the youngest at 33.

But the Cymru Premier - formerly known as the Welsh Premier League - is home to the youngest top-flight manager in Europe.

Last season, Jordan Hadaway guided Llandudno to promotion from the Cymru North. In July, he turned the grand old age of 25.

Image: He guided the club to promotion from the Cmyru North in 2025/26 (Image: Dan Whitehead)

A thirst for knowledge and a willingness to do the hard yards

Hadaway already had the presence of mind to focus on coaching, rather than playing, by 14.

He completed his Level 1 Leaders Award two days after his 16th birthday and was working towards his UEFA B Licence by 18, when he was in charge at Caerwys and working with a 41-year-old captain.

Later, he coached for the Real Madrid Foundation and, in 2024, he passed his A Licence. He counts Nigel Adkins and Robert Earnshaw among those to have helped him along the way.

Image: Llandudno's Jordan Hadaway turned 25 in July (Image: Dan Whitehead)

During his time at Caerwys, Hadaway wrote to Roy Hodgson, who was then in charge of Crystal Palace.

"He was the oldest manager in league football and I was the youngest manager in football, so my college tutor said to me 'Why don't you just write to him?'" he tells Sky Sports.

"I got an email from his personal assistant and he invited me in, but the day I was due to go down, Covid happened. By the time everything opened back up, he had been sacked!

"It was a bit of a nightmare because I really wanted to go and meet him, but I guess things happen for a reason, don't they?"

It is clear his strong work ethic has helped him progress.

Image: He still turns out for the club's reserves on occasions (Image: Dan Whitehead)

"While I was studying at Liverpool Hope University, some days I'd be up at 2.30am or 3am going to work in the bakery for a family friend as they'd lost staff because of Covid," he says.

"I'd stay there until 9.30am, go to a lecture from 11am until 2pm and then I'd coach from maybe 4pm until 9pm. It was a full-on period in my life!"

And it has not slowed down, given he now balances his part-time managerial role with a full-time role as a teacher.

Achieving the unachievable

In December 2022, Hadaway left his role as assistant manager at Cefn Druids to become Llandudno U19s manager, as well as the club's head of youth development.

By the start of the 2023/24 season, he had been named interim first-team manager of a club whos squad and staff had been decimated after its artificial playing surface was condemned by the Welsh FA.

"Everyone had walked away and we were two weeks away from starting the season," he recalls.

Image: When he became manager, he says he had one player on the books (Image: Dan Whitehead)

"The chairman said to me: 'Will you just try and keep us in the league and make sure we have a club? I don't care if we get relegated if that's what has to happen as long as we've got a team and a club at the end of it.'

"Everyone around me, I'll be honest, told me don't take it. My mum even says to me today: 'I can't believe you took that job'.

"But I saw it as an opportunity to go and try and prove people wrong at a very big club in Wales that has an amazing facility and a good fanbase.

"I had the smallest budget in the league by a country mile. I had one player two weeks before the start of the season and no management team. I had to put all that together in two weeks. We were favourites to get relegated, but I never once thought we would.

"We managed to finish 12th out of 16 and we got to a cup final that year. It's quite incredible, really."

Image: (Image: Dan Whitehead)

Two years later, he took the club one step further.

"My aim was always to be a Welsh Premier League manager by the time I was 27, 28. Did I ever think I was going to get there? No. It's amazing.

"I'm lucky I've had very good players and very good staff that have enabled me to push the club to that standard. It's not all about me, it's about everybody involved.

"I got quite emotional on that afternoon we got promoted. It was an achievement that probably will stick with me and be one of my best forever."

No rush to reach the top

Asked if he has aged beyond his years with the way his career has progressed, Hadaway quips: "Yes - I think my hairline's shown that!

"A lot of people say I'm the oldest 25-year-old they've ever met. I think I am mature, but I'm mature because of the people I've grown up around. The people you spend the most time with have the biggest impact on you."

That maturity is reflected in his attitude towards what comes next.

Many would leap to the conclusion that, if he is doing well at 25 in Wales, a career over the border in England will be on the cards soon.

That may well come to be true, but Hadaway is in no immediate rush.

"Don't get me wrong, I would love to do it [work in the Premier League or EFL]," he adds.

"However, I love my job and I love supporting young people that need the support in school, and I think it would have to be a very good opportunity to take me away from what I'm doing currently. I'm also not naive.

"But I don't think I should get given a chance because I'm the youngest manager in top-flight football - I think I should be given a chance because I'm good enough.

"If we had this interview again in 10 years' time and I was still at Llandudno, I would be happy, because I'm not someone that chases the stars. I'm someone that likes to make sure I'm doing a good job where I'm at and make sure that when I leave, I've left it in a very good place and it's stable."

For someone who has accomplished so much so young, perhaps Hadaway's strength is in knowing there is no need to rush.

Sports.title: England's Bethell out of Australia tour and a doubt for South Africa Tests
Sports.content:
Jacob Bethell has been ruled out of England's entire white-ball tour of Australia after suffering a setback on his return from injury and could now be a doubt for the Tests in South Africa.

Batter and spin bowler Bethell has not played since scoring 91 in the final one-day international against India at Lord's in July after sustaining a knee problem that required surgery.

The 23-year-old was hoping to return for the three ODIs against Australia, which start in Perth on Friday, and the five T20 internationals that follow, but will now head back to England after a problem in training and is poised to see a specialist.

Image: Bethell could also be a doubt for the Test series in South Africa from December 17

On Monday, Bethell was included in England's Test squad for the three-match tour of South Africa from December 17.

Fast bowler Josh Tongue had already been already ruled out of the Australia fixtures due to a toe injury.

England have called up uncapped Hampshire seamer Eddie Jack and Sussex all-rounder James Coles into the ODI squad as replacements for Tongue and Bethell.

Jack and Coles were already part of the T20 party.

Image: Bethell was not a shoo-in to return to the ODI side after the form of openers Tom Banton and Ben Duckett

In Bethell's absence from the ODI side, Tom Banton has formed a successful opening partnership with Ben Duckett, so his return to the XI straightaway in that format was perhaps unlikely.

If the left-hander also misses the red-ball assignments in South Africa, live on Sky Sports, then it will ease a selection dilemma for England.

Jordan Cox struck three half-centuries in as many matches after deputising for Bethell at No 3 in the 3-0 Test rout of Pakistan during the home summer.

Should Bethell be fit, there may only be space for three of him, Cox, Emilio Gay and Dan Lawrence in the XI.

Image: Uncapped Hampshire fast bowler Eddie Jack has been added to England's ODI squad

Atherton: How easy will it be for Bethell to slip back in?

Sky Sports Cricket's Michael Atherton on Jacob Bethell:

"I think it is a precautionary thing given how busy the winter is but the concern is how little cricket Bethell's had and therefore how easy is it for him to slip back into the team?

"Perhaps this makes it a bit more difficult but our best wishes to him. "Let's hope it is not a significant setback.

"There is a bit of Lions cricket just ahead of the main tour of South Africa.

"That's the good thing for him. There's a camp in Pietermaritzburg and four-day Test against South Africa A so there's an opportunity there once he's fit."

Image: Bethell missed the 3-0 Test win over Pakistan during the home summer

Sports.title: Liverpool incorrectly denied pen vs Arsenal says independent panel
Sports.content:
Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty when Jurrien Timber pulled Alexander Isak's shirt in Arsenal's victory at Anfield, an independent panel has ruled.

The Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel assesses refereeing incidents across every Premier League match and voted 4:1 that referee Andy Madley should have awarded Liverpool a spot kick.

The panel also voted 3:2 that VAR Stuart Attwell should have intervened and sent Madley to the pitchside monitor on the basis that it was a clear and obvious error.

Arsenal led 1-0 through Kai Havertz's goal, which proved to be the winner, when Isak attempted to head Bradley Barcola's cross in the 21st minute on November 1, but was pulled back by defender Timber.

One KMI panellist believed "the short-lived holding to lack clear impact on the ability of Isak to progress", while two panellists argued, "the subjectivity in assessing impact meant this did not meet the high threshold for VAR intervention".

Isak stayed on his feet during the incident and Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said afterwards he would tell the striker to go down next time.

So far this season 196 KMIs have been examined, with the correct on-field decision taken in 86 per cent of cases. That rises to 97 per cent following VAR intervention.

What is the KMI panel? The Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel provides an independent assessment of key decisions in every Premier League match.



It is an independent group of five members: three former players or coaches, one representative from the Premier League, and one from Pro Ref, the organisation responsible for refereeing in England.

What the pundits said...

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Carragher, Daniel Sturridge and Ian Wright discuss Liverpool's penalty shout after Jurrien Timber pulled Alexander Isak's shirt as the striker attempted to head the ball

Jamie Carragher: "One of the best goalscorers in the league is pulled back seven yards out and it stops him heading the ball - why does he need to make a meal of it? VAR, do your job."

Ian Wright: "He shouldn't have to make more of it. We can see it... Unless I'm pulled back, I'm going to head it as much as I can. When he pulled him, it was just about enough as he would need to go down.

"VAR is wrong in this instance. If they gave that penalty, I wouldn't sit here and say 'I can't believe they gave that'."

Gary Neville: "It's actually unnatural not to make more of it. When you get pulled and you're just about to score, you ordinarily complain like crazy. It's a very odd reaction from Isak."

Daniel Sturridge: "Unfortunately, he (Isak) has not fallen over. You're supposed to fall over, put your arms in the air and show the referee you're mad about it... to me, his reaction is almost like 'VAR, do your job'.

"But they've not done their job. He shouldn't have to make more of it - clearly, he shouldn't. Everyone can see that his arm is stretched, he [Timber] is holding him with a stretched-out arm."

Ref Watch's verdict...

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Ref Watch panel discuss whether Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty at Anfield against Arsenal, after Jurrien Timber appeared to pull the shirt of Alexander Isak

Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher: "It depends which angle you watch it from. The first angle, you see nothing. That is the referee's angle.

"The second angle, which is what VAR looks at, and it is a lot more damning.

"VAR looks at it in slow motion, which is another thing against him. In normal speed, he grabs and grabs him quickly but let's go. Does he do enough [for a penalty]?

"What is Timber's intention? He is on the wrong side of him. Does he do enough to stop him? He [Isak] will say yes, as he is close to the ball.

"VAR would be accused of re-refereeing if it is a penalty. It is a case of damned if they do and damned if they don't.

"It has to be the case of on-field. The more I watch it, the more I think he [Timber] has taken a big chance and has got lucky."

What happens if Isak goes down? "Once a player hits the ground, there are more questions to ask.

"There is asking what has knocked him down. Has he gone down by his own momentum, has he slipped or has he been pulled or pushed?

"Once you factor that in, obviously you have a different decision. He [referee] has to deal with the situation he has seen. He has seen a little pull of the jersey and thought no penalty."

Jay Bothroyd: "Where was the referee? Every angle, I can see it is a penalty.

"He has pulled his shirt. How can none of them [referee and VAR] see that and say it is a penalty? I can't comprehend that. I don't get it.

"That is one of the most obvious penalties [I have seen]. He is running forward! He has stifled his momentum going forward, to stop him heading the ball.

"Every angle I look at, even normal time, I said it could be a penalty. I look at it now, the more I see it, the more I ask myself how they have missed it! How do they lose focus and not get that."

Liverpool's view...

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking after the 1-0 defeat to Arsenal at Anfield, Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola suggested that Alexander Isak would have been awarded a penalty if he'd gone to ground and claimed that he'll be instructing his players to do so in future

Andoni Iraola: "The Isak one is a clear penalty. We can all see that he holds the t-shirt. The ball just goes one centimetre in front of Alex. Alex is going to hit the ball in front of the goal."

On whether the player needed to go down: "The fact that you are even asking me that shows he should have gone to the floor. If he does, they call the penalty 100 per cent.

Asked whether he will tell Alex to go down next time: "Yes, definitely."

Virgil van Dijk: "I've seen it back and I've seen it given as well on other occasions. Today it wasn't meant to be.

"The VAR doesn't notice it? There are 50 cameras. Even more. Why does he have to complain when there are so many cameras? It is spotted because everyone's seen it.

"In the end, it wasn't given and we lose the game unfortunately, so well done to Arsenal."

From Arsenal's perspective, Mikel Arteta said he had not watched the incident back and had no comment when asked by Sky Sports.

Mac Allister reaction 'clearly exaggerated'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Super Sunday panel discuss Alexis Mac Allister's clash with Noni Madueke where the Argentine midfielder fell to the ground after a head-to-head incident with the Arsenal winger

Towards the end of the second half, Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister went down holding his face after his forehead touched with Noni Madueke's.

VAR reviewed the incident, and the Arsenal winger was not sent off. Instead, Mac Allister was booked.

The KMI panel unanimously felt the referee was correct not to show Madueke a red card as the contact was "negligible" and Mac Allister's reaction "clearly exaggerated".

Referee and VAR missed Ipswich penalty vs Hull

The KMI panel also ruled that Ipswich Town should have been awarded a penalty in their 2-2 draw with Hull City on October 3.

Nobel Mendy was judged to have committed a holding offence against Dara O'Shea during a corner in the 18th minute, with the score still goalless.

The panel voted 4-1 that referee Tom Kirk should have awarded a penalty, while VAR Neil Davies should also have recommended an on-field review.

The majority agreed there was "a clear sustained holding offence", although one panellist felt O'Shea and Florentino Luis's actions during the incident should have been considered, meaning a penalty was not warranted.

Sports.title: From the sack in Cyprus to Liverpool: Iraola's first job explained
Sports.content:
Not every successful career starts spectacularly well but Andoni Iraola's journey to Liverpool will take some beating. Seven years ago, he was sacked from his first job in management after a winless streak in the Cypriot top division with AEK Larnaca.

Iraola learned from the experience and rebuilt his career back in Spain with Mirandes before really impressing with Rayo Vallecano and Bournemouth to earn his opportunity at Anfield. Nevertheless, it must be curious for his old colleagues to witness the rise.

Were there any believers that day in January when Larnaca drew 2-2 at home to Ermis Aradippou, the team that would go on to finish bottom of the table? It extended the run of league games without a win to six and Iraola paid the price for that streak with his job.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Liverpool's match at Crystal Palace in the Premier League

Were there clues beyond the results that Iraola was destined for bigger things and merely the victim of a trigger-happy firing culture at the Cypriot club? Speaking to David Catala, who played under him at Larnaca, including in that final game, he did see promising signs.

"He already had very clear ideas of what he wanted," Catala tells Sky Sports. "You saw it and, for sure, all the players were speaking about how he was going to become a fantastic coach. But to reach this level? To say that he would be at Liverpool? That is a big claim."

Image: David Catala celebrates scoring for Iraola's Larnaca side against Bayer Leverkusen

Iraola had spent his entire playing career in Europe at Athletic Club prior to a brief sojourn stateside with New York City. His first foray into the managerial game with Larnaca put him outside of his comfort zone, even if there was a Spanish constituency in the club.

His initial impact was impressive. Three rounds of qualifying for the Europa League group stage were successfully negotiated with wins over Dundalk, Sturm Graz and Trencin. Just as significantly, the players at Larnaca readily embraced Iraola's illuminating ideas.

"To be in the Europa League for a club in Cyprus was amazing," explains Catala. "And the work that he did was good. These were the same ideas that he wants at Liverpool, actually, pressing high and wanting to be very aggressive with and without the ball."

In Cyprus at that time, this was particularly rare. "The rhythm of the game there was very slow. I was able to play there until I was 38 years old because that rhythm was not so high." Iraola had a different vision of the game, learned under Marcelo Bielsa in Bilbao.

"When Andoni came, it changed."

Image: Andoni Iraola attempted to introduce a pressing game during his time at AEK Larnaca

Catala explains: "Everything was more explosive with him, more rhythm, more intensity. You saw how Marcelo did it with Athletic Club. I remember sometimes it was like that for us. Crazy things like following man-to-man all over the pitch. That was crazy as players."

He recognises now that it was a taste of the future of the game. "Football has gone in that direction. The way you have to press. It changed the mentality of the players." Even the game in that country. "He changed a little bit the rhythm of the league in Cyprus."

For a while, it worked. At the start of December, 10 games in, Larnaca were second in the table to Limassol, the only team to beat them during that period. Iraola's side were actually ahead of the six-time reigning champions and the eventual title winners APOEL.

But it all unravelled quickly. There was a 5-1 home defeat to Bayer Leverkusen in Europe that was sandwiched between a trio of away trips on the island that yielded no wins. A home defeat by the odd goal increased the pressure before the brief Christmas break.

A loss away to Omonia followed by that draw against strugglers Ermis sealed his fate. There were some formation tweaks but nothing major. "He did not change too much in terms of his thinking about the way of playing against different teams," recalls Catala.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at our picks of Alisson's dazzling goalkeeping display against Crystal Palace

The real lesson was that even in an environment that was supposed to be away from the spotlight for such a high-profile figure during his playing days, pressure comes quickly in football. "If you are not getting results, it is difficult to have the trust of the owners."

Catala explains: "Cyprus is very difficult for coaches, and especially for young coaches, because the owners of the football clubs, they are very passionate. And at the moment that you are not getting the results, they sack the coach like they are just peanuts.

"As soon as you lose games, especially against the lower teams, immediately the fans are speaking with the owner and the owner is going crazy. You cannot have the stability that maybe you need when you are a young coach. This is what happened to Andoni."

Liverpool

Manchester United Sunday 22nd November 4:00pm Kick off 4:30pm

For Catala, who would go on to manage Larnaca himself, lasting a little longer than Iraola, he has tried to take things from his old coach. And believes Iraola too will have benefited from that experience. "It was still a good choice to start there," he insists.

"Cyprus is not an easy place for anyone to work but it is a good place for a young coach to start their journey. He had the opportunity to coach a team in the Europa League, for example. Unfortunately, football everywhere is now very unstable for all coaches.

"It was a short period. But he would have learned many things from his experience in Cyprus about how to manage situations. It was his first job, you have to take something from that. For sure, he has improved a lot since then and he has developed himself."

Into the Liverpool coach, no less. "I am happy for him. If you look at the last years, you can see that he is obviously a fantastic coach. I cannot say that I did not expect it, but it is a little bit of a surprise." From the sack at Larnaca to Liverpool, how could it not be?

Sports.title: Manchester United close on Mauricio Pochettino deal before settling Carrick’s fate
Sports.content:
Manchester United are closing in on agreeing a deal for Mauricio Pochettino to become their head coach if Michael Carrick is sacked in line with the recommendation from Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and Omar Berrada, the chief executive, to Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

Pochettino is the US men’s national team head coach but wants the United job if, as expected, Carrick is removed.

Wilcox and Berrada are meeting Ratcliffe in Monaco, where the minority owner will be informed that Carrick should lose his job. Ratcliffe controls United’s sporting policy.

There is a growing sense among United players that Carrick will be sacked, with their expectation being that Pochettino will replace him. Pochettino has managed in the Premier League with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea.

A United board meeting is scheduled for Wednesday at which one or more of the six Glazer siblings who are the majority owners will be represented. There is an expectation within the executive and in Carrick’s camp that the sacking will be ratified there and that an announcement will follow.

Pochettino’s contract contains a release clause of about $10m (£7.5m), although the compensation United would have to pay will be higher if the Argentinian brings his own staff, including his longtime assistant and confidant Jesús Pérez, who has worked with Pochettino for 16 years.

Pochettino is due to take charge of the US in Concacaf Nations League matches against Haiti on Saturday and Wednesday in Miami and Cincinnati respectively, their first competitive fixtures of the 2030 World Cup qualifying cycle.
