World.title: Kenya’s Last Ebola Patient Goes Home
World.content:
File photo. Kenyatta National Hospital, Nairobi. (Photo: Rotsee, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

KENYA · HEALTH

Key Facts The country Kenya, an East African tourism and trade hub, is led on Ebola by Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale.

What happened Duale said on Wednesday 11 November 2026 that the last of Kenya’s seven Ebola survivors went home.

The count Kenya has confirmed nine cases and two deaths since its first imported case on 6 October.

The clock A 42-day countdown now runs until Wednesday 23 December 2026, if no new case appears.

The reach Kenya says it is open to travel and trade, and will issue no Ebola-free certificates.

Kenya’s last patient with Ebola, a deadly viral fever, left hospital on Wednesday 11 November 2026, and the country has begun the countdown that could end its outbreak on paper. Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale announced it at a press conference at the Health Ministry in Nairobi.

For US readers, the news matters because Kenya is a major gateway for safari travel, aid work and business in East Africa. It also shows how far an imported Ebola case can be contained when contacts are traced fast.

What Happened

Duale said the seventh and final patient had been discharged, and that all 135 people who had contact with the sick had finished 21 days of monitoring. He said five patients went home on 3 November, a sixth on 6 November and the last on 11 November.

Kenya’s Health Ministry counts nine confirmed cases in total, all linked to a single imported infection, with two deaths. The last new case was confirmed on 19 October, the ministry said.

At least one local outlet wrongly reported that Kenya had been declared Ebola-free. The formal status is different: the ministry itself says Kenya has only started the countdown, so the country is not yet officially declared free.

How the Countdown Works

The World Health Organization (WHO), the United Nations health agency, says symptoms of this Bundibugyo form, a rarer species of Ebola, can appear two to 21 days after infection. Health authorities wait twice that long, 42 days, before they call an outbreak over.

Duale said the period runs until Wednesday 23 December 2026. If one new case appears, the clock would have to restart.

What the Government Is Doing

Kenya will keep screening travellers at all 26 points of entry, such as airports, seaports and border posts. Rapid response teams stay on alert in every county.

The Health and Foreign Affairs ministries will soon publish an advisory for Kenyans returning from Ebola-affected areas, particularly Congo. It will require a health declaration through the ministry’s OHAI chatbot before travel, screening on arrival and 21 days of follow-up by health teams.

No Ebola-Free Certificates

Duale urged countries that imposed blanket travel and visa limits on Kenya to review and lift them. He argued that Kenya now has no patients under treatment, no contacts in quarantine and no community spread.

He also said Kenya will not serve as a quarantine centre for other countries, and will not issue quarantine or “Ebola-free” certificates for travellers. He said such documents have no basis in the International Health Regulations, the World Health Organization’s global rulebook.

Why It Matters

The outbreak is far from over in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where health authorities have reported more than 11,000 confirmed cases. Our report on the Congo figures and our earlier look at the spread in the east of the country show the scale.

Duale warned that the risk of a new imported case stays real. That is why the 42 days will be a test of Kenya’s surveillance, not a victory lap.

What It Means for You

If you plan a trip to Kenya, the government says tourism and business run normally, and it sets no limits on movement or gatherings. Check your airline and US entry rules before you fly, because other countries set their own conditions.

If you hold shares in East African travel, airline or hospitality firms, the next six weeks decide whether Kenya’s Ebola label fades. Anyone with fever, weakness, vomiting or unexplained bleeding after travel to an affected area should call the toll-free line 719.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether any new case will appear before 23 December. The text of the promised travel advisory, and its start date, have not been published yet.

It is also unclear whether countries with travel and visa limits will lift them after Duale’s appeal. We found no government reply yet.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Kenya Officially Ebola-Free Now?

Not yet. Kenya has started a 42-day countdown that runs until Wednesday 23 December 2026, and it can be declared free only if no new case appears.

How Many People Had Ebola in Kenya?

The Health Ministry counts nine confirmed cases, including two deaths. Seven patients recovered and the last one was discharged on 11 November 2026.

Is It Safe to Travel to Kenya Now?

The government says Kenya is open to tourism and trade, with no restrictions on movement. Travellers are screened at 26 entry points, and a health advisory for Kenyans returning from affected areas is due soon.

Will Kenya Issue Ebola-Free Certificates for Travel?

No. Duale said such papers have no basis in the International Health Regulations, the global health rulebook of the World Health Organization.

Sources: Ministry of Health of Kenya, press conference of Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, 11 November 2026; World Health Organization, Ebola disease fact sheet.

World.title: Nigerian Bank Lets Firms Pay China in Naira
World.content:
File photo: Tinubu Square in central Lagos, Nigeria's commercial capital. (Photo: Jeremy Weate, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

NIGERIA · BANKING

On Monday 9 November 2026, Stanbic IBTC, a Nigerian bank that is part of South Africa’s Standard Bank Group, unveiled a payment platform in Lagos. It lets Nigerian businesses start a payment in naira while the recipient in China is settled in renminbi (RMB), the Chinese currency also called the yuan.

The platform runs through CIPS, China’s Cross-Border Interbank Payment System, a clearing network for yuan payments between banks. Wole Adeniyi, Stanbic IBTC’s chief executive, said: “our group, Standard Bank Group, is a direct participant in the China cross-border interbank payment system.”

What Nigerian firms start a payment in naira; the Chinese recipient is settled in renminbi (yuan).

Route China’s Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS), where Standard Bank Group is a direct participant.

Claim The bank says CIPS settles in 24 hours what the traditional route does in 48 to 72.

Missing Fees, limits, product name and start date were not disclosed.

A Nigerian bank says businesses will be able to pay Chinese suppliers in naira and have them receive yuan, a small example of how African trade with China is settled.

Why It Matters

Jesuseun Fatoyinbo, the bank’s Head of Transaction Banking, described CIPS as “a purpose built clearing and settlement rail for international RMB payment”. He said the platform could reduce transaction costs.

The bank says a payment that took 48 to 72 hours by the traditional route can be done through CIPS in 24 hours, which is a company claim not independently verified. No official figure on yuan payment volumes in Nigeria is available yet.

File photo. Central Lagos seen from above, September 2018. (Photo: Subomi07, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

In Plain English The naira is Nigeria’s currency and the renminbi, or yuan, is China’s. CIPS is a network for yuan transfers between banks. Stanbic IBTC is a Nigerian bank, and Standard Bank Group is its South African parent. The platform is one product of that group, not a new bank.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Who Can Use It

The bank aims the service at Nigerian importers, manufacturers and others who regularly pay Chinese suppliers. It has not published eligibility rules.

Standard Bank Group has been building its access to CIPS, as our earlier piece on its yuan clearing role explains. Its Tanzanian arm launched direct yuan settlement in August 2026.

What the Central Bank Said

The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), the country’s monetary authority, sent a message from Aderinola Shonekan, Director of its Trade and Exchange Department. Nnenna Ezekannagha, an Assistant Director, delivered it at the launch.

The CBN message welcomed the launch and linked it to the central bank’s policy of currency diversification. The reports of the launch included no figures.

What to Watch Next

No start date for the service has been given. The next checkpoint is an announcement of fees, limits and a launch date.

Wider Nigerian developments are on our Nigeria news hub. Pricing, once published, will show how attractive the route is.

What Is Not Known

The bank has not disclosed fees, transaction limits, a formal product name or the date the service starts. It has also not published a naira-per-yuan rate.

No official figure for Nigeria-China trade was obtained for this report. Whether every payment avoids the US dollar is not confirmed, and no link to any currency swap between the two central banks has been stated.

What It Means for You

The people directly affected are Nigerian importers and exporters, and the banks that serve them. For context on the currency, see our latest naira market report.

For readers in the United States who follow the dollar’s role in trade, this is a small example of yuan settlement spreading in African trade finance with China. It is one platform from one bank, and the facts so far do not show how widely it will be used.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Stanbic IBTC naira to yuan platform?

It is a cross-border payment service unveiled in Lagos on Monday 9 November 2026. Nigerian businesses start a payment in naira and the recipient in China is settled in renminbi.

How does the platform work?

It runs through CIPS, China’s Cross-Border Interbank Payment System, where Standard Bank Group is a direct participant. The bank says CIPS can settle in 24 hours what the traditional route does in 48 to 72.

How much will the service cost?

The bank has not disclosed fees, limits or a start date. It says only that the service could reduce transaction costs.

Sources: Stanbic IBTC, statements at the launch, 9 November 2026; Central Bank of Nigeria, remarks delivered at the launch, 9 November 2026.

World.title: Blast Hits Celsia Power Plant in Colombia
World.content:
Cali, Colombia's third-largest city, seen from the hills above it; file photo, January 2016. (Photo: Hectorangelazul, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

COLOMBIA · ENERGY

An explosive device went off at a hydroelectric plant in Colombia on Tuesday 10 November 2026, according to the company that owns it. Celsia, a Colombian power company listed on the Colombia Stock Exchange, says nobody was hurt.

Celsia says two armed men attacked its Amaime plant, a small station of 19.9 megawatts (MW, a unit of power output) in the municipality of Palmira, in Valle del Cauca, a Colombian department, or province. The company calls the act terrorist and says it is assessing the damage.

World.title: Chile Deputies Seek Probe of State Oil Firm
World.content:
Chile's National Congress building in Valparaíso, pictured on 3 September 2023. The Chamber of Deputies, which would vote first on an impeachment case, meets there. The photo does not show the 2026 dispute. Photo: Carlos Figueroa Rojas / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

CHILE · ENERGY

Deputies in Chile’s lower house are pushing for a special inquiry into ENAP (Empresa Nacional del Petróleo), the state oil company that runs the Concón refinery on the Valparaíso coast. The push follows Chile’s environmental regulator, the SMA, which charged the company over allegedly false pollution reporting.

Jaime Mulet and Hotuiti Teao have backed the request, which needs 62 of the chamber’s 155 deputies to become a commission. The number of signatures is not known beyond the position of 27 October.

Deputies in Chile’s lower house want an official inquiry into whether the state oil company misreported sulfur pollution, after the environmental regulator brought two of its gravest charges.

Why It Matters

A commission can summon ministers, officials and staff of state-owned companies, and under Chile’s Constitution they must appear and hand over information. That puts public pressure on a company the state owns.

No macro figure bears directly on this story. ENAP’s earlier results are covered in our ENAP profit report.

In Plain English ENAP is Chile’s state-owned oil company, and ENAP Refinerías is the unit that runs the Concón refinery. The SMA is the regulator that checks whether companies obey environmental rules. A special investigative commission is a group of deputies that questions officials and writes a report. Sulfur dioxide is a polluting gas, and the SMA says ENAP’s reports on it were false or incomplete.

What the Deputies Want

Mulet, of the Federación Regionalista Verde Social, a regional and green party, called the charges “extremely serious” on Tuesday 27 October 2026. He asked colleagues, especially from the Valparaíso Region, to sign the request.

At that point only Teao, a deputy from the Valparaíso Region, had signed. The commission would look at criminal, internal and political responsibilities.

File photo, January 2021. A flare stack burning gas at the ENAP plant in Concón, Valparaíso Region; the photo predates the charges and does not show the conduct alleged. (Photo: Mediabanco Agencia, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

What the Regulator Charged

On Monday 26 October 2026 the Superintendencia del Medio Ambiente (SMA), Chile’s environmental regulator, brought four charges against ENAP Refinerías. That is the unit that runs the Aconcagua refinery in Concón, a coastal town in the Valparaíso Region, and two are preliminarily classed “gravísimos”, the most serious grade.

The charges concern allegedly false or incomplete information on sulfur recovery and sulfur dioxide emissions. The SMA recalculated recovery efficiency at 94.1% in 2023, 90.5% in 2024 and 90.2% in 2025, against a required minimum of 98%.

The SMA says flaring was left out of reports, so emissions were 1,277 tonnes in 2023 and 1,168 tonnes in 2024. The annual limit is 1,145 tonnes.

The maximum fine is 22,000 UTA (Unidad Tributaria Anual, an inflation-linked Chilean tax unit), about US$19 million. A charge is an accusation ENAP can contest, not a finding of guilt.

How ENAP and the Government Replied

ENAP says it found the inconsistencies itself and activated internal controls in January 2026. It says it has “zero tolerance” for the conduct.

The company also says air-quality monitors near the refinery have shown no breach of the sulfur dioxide or fine-particle standards since 2019. It has 15 business days to file a compliance plan and 22 business days for its defence.

Both deadlines were extended by the regulator on its own initiative, and we could not find their start date. The Energy and Finance ministries called the facts “unacceptable”.

What to Watch Next

The first checkpoint is whether the request reaches 62 of 155 deputies and is formally filed. The second is the SMA’s next step, which follows once ENAP files its compliance plan and defence.

What Is Not Known

It is not known how many signatures the request has gathered since 27 October, or whether it has been formally filed. ENAP’s reply to the request was not found, and it is not known whether the SMA has set a fine.

What It Means for You

ENAP is owned by the Chilean state, so the people most affected are Chilean taxpayers and residents near Concón. For a US reader the direct exposure is limited, because ENAP is a state company rather than a listed stock.

Anyone following Chile’s energy sector should watch the commission request and the SMA’s decision. More coverage is on our Chile news hub.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the ENAP investigative commission?

It is a request by deputies for a special commission on ENAP, Chile’s state oil company. It would look at criminal, internal and political responsibilities.

How many deputies are needed to create it?

Article 52 of Chile’s Constitution requires at least two-fifths of deputies in office. With 155 deputies, that is 62.

Has ENAP been fined?

We have not confirmed any fine, because the SMA has so far brought charges only. The maximum fine is 22,000 UTA, about US$19 million.

World.content:

BRAZIL · COMPANIES

Key Facts The company TIM S.A. is a Brazilian mobile carrier with 61.6 million mobile customers.

The profit Net profit fell 18% to about US$178 million in the third quarter.

The sales Revenue rose 5.3% to about US$1.27 billion, with fixed-service revenue up 30%.

The US link TIM’s shares trade in São Paulo and in New York, under the ticker TIMB.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 74.2 points (November 2026 edition).

TIM, a major Brazilian mobile carrier, earned 18% less net profit in the third quarter of 2026, even as its sales grew. Net profit fell to R$991 million (about US$178 million) from R$1,208 million (about US$216 million) a year earlier.

For US readers, TIM matters because its American depositary receipts, or ADRs, trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker TIMB. ADRs are US-traded certificates that stand for shares of a foreign company.

What Happened

TIM S.A. published its third-quarter results after the market closed on Monday 9 November 2026. Net revenue rose 5.3% to R$7.07 billion (about US$1.27 billion), and the company said the results keep it in line with its 2026 targets.

WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Normalised EBITDA, a measure of operating earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation that strips out one-off items, rose 6.7% to R$3,701 million (about US$663 million). Its margin, the share of revenue left as operating earnings, widened 0.7 points to 52.4%.

Reported EBITDA, with the one-off items left in, rose only 0.5% to R$3,486 million (about US$625 million). The gap is mostly a R$207 million (about US$37 million) one-off fair-value accounting adjustment tied to TIM’s purchase of I-Systems, a company it acquired, plus R$7.8 million (about US$1.4 million) of consulting fees.

Normalised net profit fell 7.8% to R$1,113 million (about US$199 million), or R$0.47 per share (about US$0.08). A year earlier it was R$0.50 per share.

Where Growth Came From

Mobile service revenue rose 4.0% to R$6.45 billion (about US$1.16 billion). Customers on monthly postpaid plans grew 5.2% to 34.0 million, while prepaid customers, who pay as they go, fell 9.0% to 27.6 million.

Fixed service revenue jumped 30.1% to R$430 million (about US$77 million). TIM Ultrafibra, its home broadband service, reached 931,000 customers (up 13.2%).

Fixed revenue also reflects V8. Tech, a technology company TIM now consolidates.

TIM said stronger competition, especially in the first half, led to bigger discounts to keep customers. It also said that price rises applied through the year helped revenue.

Why Profit Fell

TIM declared R$515 million (about US$92 million) in interest on capital, a tax-deductible way for Brazilian companies to pay shareholders, against R$800 million (about US$143 million) a year earlier. That shrank its tax shield, and income tax and social contribution, a profit-linked levy, rose on a reported basis to R$70 million (about US$13 million) from R$13 million (about US$2 million).

Net financial expense rose 18.0% to R$525 million (about US$94 million), mainly because of higher interest on leases and lower interest income on cash. Depreciation and amortisation also rose after TIM consolidated I-Systems.

Cash and Debt

Operating free cash flow, the cash left after operating costs and investment, rose 3.0% to R$1,876 million (about US$336 million). Capital spending was R$978 million (about US$175 million), up 0.4%.

Total net debt, which is borrowings minus cash and includes lease obligations, was R$11.1 billion (about US$1.99 billion), or 0.78 times normalised EBITDA. TIM announced or paid R$1.56 billion (about US$280 million) in interest on capital and share buybacks through September.

For earlier coverage of Brazil’s mobile market, see our reports on Vivo’s second-quarter profit and on Claro and its parent América Móvil. Both help put TIM’s results in context.

What It Means for You

If you hold TIM’s ADRs or Brazil funds, the quarter shows a carrier that is growing sales and cash flow while higher taxes and financing costs squeeze profit. The quarter also shows how much TIM’s profit depends on the size of its interest-on-capital payments.

The shift from prepaid to postpaid plans points to customers moving to monthly contracts, which usually bring steadier revenue. Competition for those customers is already costing TIM in discounts.

What Is Not Known

It is not yet clear whether TIM will declare more interest on capital before the year ends, which would cut its tax bill again. It is also not known how much of the revenue growth comes from price rises that competitors may match.

It is also not clear how much V8. Tech and I-Systems added to growth on their own.

How profit moves in the fourth quarter will depend on taxes and financing costs as much as on sales.

Frequently Asked Questions

How Much Profit Did TIM Make?

Net profit was R$991 million (about US$178 million) in the third quarter of 2026, down 18% from a year earlier. Normalised net profit, which strips out one-off items, was R$1,113 million (about US$199 million).

Why Did TIM’s Profit Fall?

TIM declared less interest on capital, which raised its income tax bill. Its net financial expense also rose 18.0%, and an accounting adjustment from the I-Systems purchase hit reported earnings.

Where Does TIM Trade in the United States?

TIM’s American depositary receipts trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker TIMB. Its shares trade in São Paulo as TIMS3.

How Many Customers Does TIM Have?

TIM had 61.6 million mobile customers at the end of September 2026, down 1.7% from a year earlier. Postpaid customers rose 5.2% to 34.0 million, while prepaid customers fell 9.0% to 27.6 million.
